what.short: The trusted implementation of fork_join: run the left thunk on a new domain and the right one here, join, and cast the joined result back to unique.
long: `fork_join left right` spawns `left` with `Domain.Safe.spawn`, runs `right` on the calling domain, and joins the spawned domain before returning or re-raising, so the domain never outlives the call. The only unchecked step is `Obj.magic_unique` on the joined result: `Domain.join` returns its value `aliased`, and the cast is justified because the domain handle is private, joined once, and its domain has exited.

The module has no refinements and nothing in it is proved; it is part of the trusted base of the parallel [quicksort](demo:quicksort), which uses it to sort the two sides of a partition on owned arrays.

notes.title: The one unchecked step
notes.text: If `right` raises, the spawned domain is still joined (its own exception ignored) before the original exception is re-raised with its backtrace. `Obj.magic_unique` restores the uniqueness that `Domain.join` forgets; this is sound only because `domain` is joined exactly once and never escapes.

what.short: Trusted externals that restate Pref's token operations with ghost tokens, so that ownership is erased and only the cell operations remain at run time.
long: The types are `Pref`'s (`'a t`, `'a token`, `'a heap`, `Heap`); what changes is the mode. `own`, `empty`, `read`, `write`, `split`, `join` and `alloc` take and return their tokens `@ ghost`, and `partition` is a boxed record with two ghost fields where `Pref` uses an unboxed pair. Each is an `external` over the same C primitives in `runtime/pref.c` (`split` has its own bytecode stub, `caml_pref_ghost_split_bytecode`), so every contract here is assumed.

Code that keeps ownership only in proofs uses this module: the locks and one-shot channels, raw memory and the LZ4 buffers, the e-graph owner, the flat hash table's storage and the union–find forest. `alloc` is declared with `val` in `ghost_pref.mli` and is an `external` here, which the shared trust page lists among the trusted token operations.

notes.title: Allocation with a ghost token
notes.text: The fresh handle is not in the old heap, and the new token's heap is the old one with the handle bound to `value`. Only `value` and the handle exist at run time; the token argument and the `state` field are erased.

what.short: The trusted primitives behind Unique_cell: create, take, put and replace for a cell holding a unique payload, specified by a ghost heap of payload snapshots.
long: `Make (V)` models a cell's contents as `V.model option`: `Some (V.snapshot v)` when it holds `v`, `None` when empty. `take` requires a full cell and returns the payload together with a token whose heap marks the cell empty; `put` requires an empty cell; `replace` swaps. `Slot` is the same storage with a `bool` occupancy model and no snapshot, so the payload keeps its refinement through the type parameter.

Every operation is an `external` over `runtime/pref.c` (`caml_unique_cell_create`, `_take`, `_put`, `_replace`); the interface re-exports them as `val`, so only `location` looks external to a client. They are trusted: the one-shot channels, `Unique_lock` and [the channel demo](demo:one-shot-channels) rely on these contracts together with those of `Verified_atomic`.

notes.title: Taking the payload out
notes.text: The precondition requires the token to own the cell and the cell to be full; the result says the payload's snapshot is what the cell held, and the new token owns the cell as empty. In C, `take` writes `()` into the cell's slot, so the moved value has no second reference.

notes.title: An empty slot is a cell created with ()
notes.text: `Slot.empty` binds the same `caml_unique_cell_create` primitive at type `unit ->`, so an empty slot physically holds `()`. The `false` occupancy in the ghost heap is what forbids a `take` before a `put`.

what.short: The trusted atomic operations: integer load, compare-and-set, exchange, set and fetch-and-add, each opening a user invariant at its atomic step.
long: `Make (I)` repeats the declarations of `verified_atomic.mli`: every operation is an `external` over `runtime/pref.c`, so the whole module is trusted. An atomic is created from a ghost key and a token satisfying `I.holds key initial`. Each operation takes a ghost postcondition `post`, the caller's token, and a total ghost transition; the transition receives the invariant's resource at the value `before` of the atomic event and the caller's resource, and must return a `transfer` that restores `I.holds` at the new value and satisfies `post` for the outgoing resource.

This is the one place where concurrent semantics enter the library: `Spin_lock` and `One_shot` are verified against these contracts, and the [lock](demo:reference-locks) and [channel](demo:one-shot-channels) demos inherit them as assumptions. Nothing is derived from a memory model; the header comment in the interface states that the operations are strong and sequentially consistent.

notes.title: Compare-and-set opens the invariant
notes.text: The transition is called with the atomic's value `before`; it must re-establish `I.holds` at `desired` when `before = expected` and at `before` otherwise, and hand the caller a resource satisfying `post (before = expected)`. The result pairs the boolean with that resource, so a client learns from `post` what it now owns.

what.short: The verified spin-lock protocol shared by both locks: one flag whose invariant owns the full guarded cell at 0 and nothing at 1.
long: `Make (C)` builds a lock over any cell with a ghost location and a `full` predicate. It instantiates `Verified_atomic.Make` with `Invariant.holds`: flag 0 with a heap that is exactly the full cell (`good`), or flag 1 with the empty heap. `try_acquire` is one `compare_and_set` from 0 to 1 and `release` one from 1 to 0; the ghost transitions `acquire_transfer` and `release_transfer` swap the invariant's resource with the caller's.

Everything here is checked against the trusted `Verified_atomic` contract. The proof shows more than the interface exports: `release_post` requires the compare-and-set to succeed, so `release` always resets the flag, but `spin_lock.mli` only states that the returned token is empty. Both `Reference_lock` and `Unique_lock` are instances; see [the lock demo](demo:reference-locks).

notes.title: The lock invariant
notes.from: (* The lock's invariant: flag 0 with the full cell, or flag 1 with nothing. *)
notes.text: The key is a ghost record holding the cell, so the invariant can name it. Flag 0 means the lock itself owns the full cell; flag 1 means a holder does. Mutual exclusion follows from this and the ownership model: two live tokens never own the same cell.

notes.title: The acquire transition
notes.text: At the atomic step the transition gives the invariant the caller's empty resource and the caller the invariant's. If the flag was 0 that resource is the full cell, and the invariant at the new value 1 holds with the empty heap; otherwise both are empty and nothing changes hands.

notes.title: Release always succeeds
notes.text: The caller hands in a token that owns the full cell. The invariant at flag 0 would own that same cell, which is disjoint from the caller's, so the flag must be 1; `release_post` records `success`, but the exported result type keeps only that the returned token is empty.

what.short: A spin lock guarding a nonnegative int cell: Spin_lock.Make over a Ghost_pref handle, with read_owned and an unspecified try_increment.
long: `Cell` makes the guarded cell an `int Ghost_pref.t` whose payload is full when it is nonnegative, and `L = Spin_lock.Make (Cell)` supplies the protocol. `make` allocates the cell with `Ghost_pref.alloc` and hands its token to `L.create`; `read_owned` reads the value with a borrowed token that `owned` proves holds exactly this cell. All of it is verified; the atomic and cell primitives underneath are trusted.

`try_increment` acquires, adds one unless that would overflow, writes, re-proves `owned` and releases. Its body is checked, but its type `t -> bool` exports no contract. This is the `Reference_lock` of [the lock demo](demo:reference-locks).

notes.title: Why the functor's operations are wrapped
notes.from: (* [owned], [try_acquire] and [release] are the functor's. The last two are
notes.text: Signature matching compares refinements syntactically, and the functor's contracts mention `L.owned` where the interface says `owned`. The module therefore restates `try_acquire` and `release` with the interface's types and proves `owned_def` from the functor's version.

notes.title: An increment checked without a contract
notes.text: The overflow guard keeps the value nonnegative, which `release` requires through `owned`. `P.Heap.put_law` shows the written heap is still exactly the one cell. None of this reaches the interface: clients of `try_increment` learn only a `bool`.

what.short: A spin lock guarding a unique payload: Spin_lock.Make over a Unique_cell, with take and put for the holder.
long: `Make (V)` stores the payload in `Unique_cell.Make (V)`. `Spec` makes the cell's location its ghost location and calls it full when it holds `Some _`, so the lock's invariant owns a full cell. The holder moves the payload out with `take`, which leaves the cell empty, and must `put` one back before `release`, whose precondition `owned` requires a full cell.

The protocol, `make`, `take` and `put` are verified against the trusted `Unique_cell` and `Verified_atomic` contracts. Like `Reference_lock`, the module restates the functor's contracts in its own terms because signature matching compares refinements syntactically. It is the `Unique_lock` of [the lock demo](demo:reference-locks), whose rejected program releases after a `take` without a `put`.

notes.title: The guarded cell
notes.from: (* The guarded cell is a unique cell, full when it holds a payload. *)
notes.text: The payload model is `Cell.contents`, a snapshot option. Fullness is `Some _`, so an acquired lock hands out a full cell and a release demands one.

notes.title: Moving the payload
notes.to: ghost_ (location_def a); Cell.put (L.cell a) value t
notes.text: `take` and `put` are the cell's operations restated at the lock's `location`. After `take` the token owns an empty cell, which `owned` rejects, so the holder cannot release until `put` refills it.

what.short: Verified one-shot channels: a Unique_cell.Slot and an atomic flag whose invariant owns nothing at 0 and the full slot at 1.
long: `create` allocates an empty `Slot` and an atomic whose `Invariant.holds` is: flag 0 with the empty heap (the sender owns the empty slot), or flag 1 with exactly the full slot. `send` puts the payload in the slot and makes one compare-and-set from 0 to 1, handing the full slot to the invariant. `recv` calls `await`, which retries a compare-and-set from 1 to 0, with `Domain.cpu_relax` between attempts, and takes the payload with the resource that the successful step hands it.

The module is checked against the trusted contracts of `Verified_atomic` and `Unique_cell.Slot`. Endpoints are unique records, so each is used at most once, and the payload's refinement travels in the type parameter. `await` is recursive and partial: `recv` may spin forever. See [the one-shot channel demo](demo:one-shot-channels).

notes.title: The flag invariant
from: (* Zero leaves the slot with an endpoint; one owns the published payload. *)
notes.text: At 0 the invariant owns nothing and the sender's `permission` owns the empty slot; at 1 it owns the slot marked full. `recv` can therefore take from the slot only after a compare-and-set that saw 1.

notes.title: Sending cannot fail
notes.from: let send (type a : value mod portable contended)
notes.text: The sender owns the full slot when the compare-and-set runs, so the invariant at 1, which would own the same slot, cannot hold: the flag is 0. `publication_post` requires success, so the checker proves the step always succeeds and the result is discarded.

notes.title: Receiving: spin until the flag is 1
notes.from: let rec await : ('a : value mod portable contended).
notes.text: On success `reception_post` gives the caller the full slot, which is exactly `Slot.take`'s precondition. On failure the caller receives an empty heap and tries again; nothing bounds the number of attempts.

what.short: Sends ownership of one raw-memory byte to a worker domain over one-shot channels and gets back a receipt that records the byte written.
long: An owned slot is a raw-memory block, an in-bounds index and a ghost token that owns that byte. `fill` writes the byte and returns a receipt, preserving the rest of the owned heap. `dispatch` sends a slot to a worker and returns a one-shot receiver for its filled receipt. `read_receipt` reads the promised value and returns the slot with its heap unchanged.

The code is verified against the `One_shot`, `Raw_memory` and `Ghost_pref` contracts. It is the byte-buffer protocol of [the one-shot channel demo](demo:one-shot-channels), run by `testsuite/tests/vox/channel_buffer_demo.ml`.

notes.title: A receipt carries the written byte
notes.from: type owned : value mod portable contended = {s : slot | 0 <= s.index
notes.text: `owned` ties the ghost permission to the byte's location; `filled` adds that the owned heap binds it to `Some expected`. Both are refinement types, so they cross domains as channel payloads with their facts intact.

notes.title: Channel types refined by the call's arguments
notes.text: The local `Protocol` ties each job and reply to this call’s block, index and value. The returned receipt owns the selected byte and states its value. The caller receives it with `C.recv` and joins the worker through `worker`.

what.short: Raw byte buffers: trusted malloc, read, write and free over ghost per-byte locations, and verified lemmas about footprints and coverage.
long: Each block `p` has ghost locations `location p i`: index -1 is the permission to free, nonnegative indices are bytes, modelled as `byte option` (`None` for uninitialized). `malloc` may fail with `None`; on success the token gains the block's `footprint`. `read` needs an owned, initialized byte; `write` needs an owned byte; `free` needs the -1 permission and every byte (`covers`). These operations, `length`, `equal`, `location` and `location_law` are `external`s over `runtime/pref.c` and are trusted; native reads and writes are unchecked builtins whose bounds come from the refinements.

The definitions `range`, `footprint` and `covers` and the lemmas `range_at`, `footprint_at`, `covers_get`, `covers_intro`, `allocated_covers`, `write_covers`, `split_covers` and `join_covers` are verified, by induction on the upper bound. Raw memory backs the [LZ4](demo:lz4) codec's buffers, `Channel_buffer` and the unique-lock buffer client.

notes.title: Ghost locations and the trusted location law
notes.from: (* These locations exist only in the ownership model. Index -1 is the
notes.text: `location` is erased; `location_law` is assumed: it states that locations are injective in the block and the index. It is bound to the generic heap-law stub, so its truth rests on the stated contract alone.

notes.title: Allocation and freeing
notes.text: `malloc` adds a footprint disjoint from what the caller owns; `free` removes it and requires `covers` for every byte, so a block cannot be freed while another token owns any part of it.

notes.title: Splitting coverage of a range
notes.text: Restricting a heap to `range p lo mid` covers `[lo, mid)` and excluding it covers `[mid, hi)`. With `join_covers`, this is how a client divides a buffer between owners, for example across domains, and puts it back together before `free`.

what.short: Borrowed slices and owned arrays modelled by iarrays with int indices: trusted handle primitives and verified swap, split_at, split3, parallel and with_mut.
long: This is the `int`-indexed counterpart of `Borrow`: a loan's `current` and `final` models are `'a iarray`s and its laws use `Vox_iarray.slice`, `at` and `updated`. The `external`s in `Raw`, `Slice` (`length`, `get`, `set`, `snapshot`) and `Owned_array` (`of_iarray`, `into_iarray`, `get`, `set` and the unboxed `get_int`/`set_int`) are trusted contracts over `runtime/borrow.c`. The facts that link a loan to its frame and owner at `open_`, `restore`, `split`, `recombine`, `finish` and `transfer` are not in these types: the verifier adds them by primitive name in `normal_borrow_transition` ([vox_vc.ml](src:verification/vox_vc.ml)).

`Slice.swap`, `split_at`, `split3`, `finish`, `parallel` and `Owned_array.with_mut` are verified against those primitives. Only `swap` is `total`: the others create or end loans. `parallel` runs two slice callbacks, on a new domain when `spawn` is true, and returns both callbacks' postconditions on the loans' final values. Users include the iarray variant of [quicksort](demo:quicksort) (`testsuite/tests/vox/quicksort_iarray.ml`) and the [Hindley–Milner](demo:hindley-milner) inference in `hm_routed_infer.ml`, which uses `Owned_array`.

notes.title: Handle primitives with built-in meanings
notes.text: `open_` and `restore` have no refinements here, yet `with_mut` proves that the loan starts at the owner's contents and that the restored owner holds the loan's final value. Those equations come from `normal_borrow_transition` in the verifier, which recognizes `caml_borrow_open`, `caml_borrow_restore` and the other transitions. Only the declarations in `Borrow`, `Borrow_iarray` and `Vox_string_view` carry these meanings (`Vox_type.carries_builtin_meaning`); an `external` elsewhere that names the same symbol gets none.

notes.title: Splitting a loan for a callback
notes.text: The body gets two loans whose current models are the two slices and must return a result satisfying `post` on their final models. After `Raw.recombine`, the whole loan's current model is the concatenation of those finals, so `post` is restated on slices of it and the final model is unchanged. It is not `total`: `Raw.split` creates the two loans' final models.

notes.title: Two slices in parallel
notes.text: `Raw.transfer` turns the local left loan into a global one so the spawned domain can own it. The join goes through `await_both`, which joins the domain even if the right callback raises. `parallel` is not declared `total`.

what.short: Ghost credit tokens with unbounded Bigint balances: a void record with one ghost field, and verified tick, split, merge and Budget.create.
long: `Make ()` defines `token` as a record whose only field, `balance`, is a ghost nonnegative `Bigint.t`, so a token has void layout and costs nothing at run time. `credits` reads the balance; `tick`, `split`, `merge` and `empty` are defined directly on the record and verified against their contracts. With unbounded balances, `merge` needs no overflow precondition, unlike `Vox_credits`, whose balance is a machine `int`.

Each application of the generative functor gives a fresh abstract `token` type; `Budget.create` issues positive credit and is withheld from `S`, so code that receives only `S` cannot mint credit. [Online union–find](demo:online-union-find) pays its fees with these tokens.

notes.title: A token is its ghost balance
notes.to: type partition = { left : token @@ ghost; right : token @@ ghost }
notes.text: `amount` refines `Bigint.t` to nonnegative values, so every token's balance is nonnegative by construction and `nonnegative` needs only the definition of `credits`. Uniqueness of tokens, checked by the mode system, is what stops a balance from being spent twice.

what.short: Verified merge sort: split, merge and a depth-indexed recursion that spends at most size × depth comparison credits.
long: `Make (O) (C) (Compare)` sorts immutable lists. `split` alternates elements into two halves of sizes ⌈n/2⌉ and ⌊n/2⌋ and proves a permutation. `merge` calls `Compare.compare` once for each element it emits while both lists are nonempty and spends at most `length left + length right` credits. `sort_at_depth size depth` requires `size <= power depth` and `size * depth` credits: it splits the token for the left half with `C.split`, recombines with `C.merge`, and pays for the final merge with the remaining `size` credits. `sort` starts it at `Vox_sort_cost.height n`, whose bound makes `budget n` enough.

Everything is verified, including termination (`[@@decreases]` on the combined length and on `size`). The lemmas for one step are in [vox_merge_proofs.ml](src:verification/library/vox_merge_proofs.ml), and sortedness and permutation come from `Vox_ordered_sequence`. See [the merge sort demo](demo:merge-sort).

notes.title: Merge pays one credit per comparison
notes.from: let rec (merge @ total) : (left : O.elt list) @ immutable ->
notes.text: The precondition asks for at least `length left + length right` credits; the postcondition says at most that many were spent. `O.totality x y` lets the checker conclude, in the `else` branch, that `y` precedes `x`.

notes.title: Splitting the budget between the halves
notes.from: let left_budget = ghost_ (Bigint.mul left_size next_depth) in
notes.to: let combined = C.merge left_state right_state in
notes.text: The left call gets `left_size * (depth - 1)` credits and the right call the rest. The inline assertion states the accounting identity `size * depth = size + left_size * (depth - 1) + right_size * (depth - 1)`: what is left after both recursive calls covers the merge. `C.split` and `C.merge` run outside `ghost_`, so the calls remain after erasure with their token arguments removed.

what.short: Verified lemmas for one merge sort step: head and right_head for merging, lower for bounds, and split_step for the permutation of a split.
long: `Make (O) (P)` is parameterized by the order and by `Vox_ordered_sequence.Make (O)`. `head` shows that prepending the smaller head to a sorted merged tail keeps it sorted and a permutation; `right_head` does the same when the right head is smaller, using `permutation_rotate`; `lower` turns `O.le first second` and sortedness into `P.all`; `split_step` shows that moving two elements onto the two halves preserves the permutation.

All lemmas are ghost, total and checked; their statements are implications written as `if premise then conclusion else true`. They are called only from [vox_merge_sort.ml](src:verification/library/vox_merge_sort.ml) in [the merge sort demo](demo:merge-sort).

notes.title: Permutation by counting
notes.from: let (split_step @ total) (x : O.elt @ immutable) (y : O.elt @ immutable)
notes.text: `P.count_extensional` concludes a permutation from a total ghost function that proves equal counts at every element; here each count is unfolded one cons at a time. This is the usual way the library proves permutations without an inductive permutation relation.

what.short: The list theory behind Vox_sequence: recursive definitions with generated _def equations, proved laws, and the For_all, Map and Fold functors.
long: `append`, `at`, `set`, `take`, `drop`, `sub`, `from_iarray` and `of_iarray` are `let[@def]` definitions, so each gets an `_def` equation that proofs call explicitly. The laws (`append_associative`, `cut`, `drop_add`, `decompose3`, `extensional` and others) are total ghost functions proved by structural recursion. `For_all (P)`, `Map (F)` and `Fold (F)` lift a named predicate, function or step over lists with their own laws, so these operations can appear in refinements without passing functions as SMT data.

Two items are trusted: `length` is an `external` whose meaning the verifier states directly (so `length_def` is proved by `()`), and `iarray_get` binds `%array_safe_get` as a total function under an in-bounds refinement. The module is used by most list-based demos, including [HTTP](demo:http), [merge sort](demo:merge-sort) and [the functional queue](demo:functional-queue).

notes.title: length is built in
notes.text: `caml_vox_sequence_length` is one of the checker's built-in meanings: the verifier asserts the unfolding for `[]` and `::`, so `length_def` needs no proof steps. Lengths are `Bigint.t`, so no law about them needs an overflow side condition.

notes.title: Lifting a predicate over a list
notes.text: `holds` is defined by recursion on the list, and `get` specializes it to one index; `intro` (below) builds it from a total pointwise proof. `filter` and its laws live in the same functor.

notes.title: List extensionality, proved
notes.text: Two lists with equal length and equal `at` at every nonnegative index are logically equal. The proof recurses on both lists and shifts the index proof by one; `Vox_iarray` states the corresponding fact for iarrays as a trusted `external`.

what.short: The iarray theory behind Vox_iarray: at, updated, slice, swap and to_list with proved laws, For_all, and the sorting and counting theory in Int.
long: `at`, `updated`, `slice`, `swap` and `to_list` are `let[@def]` definitions over three primitives. The laws (`set_read`, `updated_read`, `slice_read`, `slice_slice`, `swap_read`, the `to_list_*` bridge to `Vox_sequence`) are proved. `For_all (P)` provides `range`, `holds`, `intro`, `get` and slice and update laws. `Int` defines `sorted`, `ordered`, `count`, `bag` and `permutation` on `int iarray`s and proves, among others, `sorted_glue` (recombining partitions around a pivot) and `permutation_swap`; `permutation` is defined through `to_list` and `Vox_int_sequence.bag`.

Trusted: `get` binds `%array_safe_get` as a total function under an in-bounds refinement; `set` and `sub` are `external`s whose types give only the result length, and the verifier supplies their element-wise meaning by primitive name (`caml_vox_iarray_set`, `caml_vox_iarray_sub` in `vox_vc.ml`); `extensional` is assumed. The theory is used by [sparse arrays](demo:sparse-arrays), [e-graphs](demo:egraphs), [Hindley–Milner](demo:hindley-milner) and `Borrow_iarray`.

notes.title: Trusted primitives
notes.text: `extensional` is assumed: two iarrays with equal length and equal `at` everywhere are logically equal. `set` and `sub` state only lengths here; their read-after-write and slice meanings are built into the verifier, which is what makes `set_read` and `slice_read` provable in one step.

notes.title: Gluing sorted partitions
notes.text: If the elements left of `index` are sorted and at most the pivot, those right of it are sorted and at least the pivot, and the pivot sits at `index`, the whole array is sorted. The proof goes through `sorted_intro` with a case split on where each adjacent pair falls; `quicksort_iarray_model.ml` uses it to recombine partitions.

what.short: Integer list theory: bounds, sortedness, and permutation as equality of insertion-sorted bags, with a proof that equal counts imply permutation.
long: `all`, `range`, `sorted`, `insert`, `bag`, `count` and `insert_all` are `let[@def]` definitions over `Vox_sequence`. `permutation left right` is `bag left === bag right`, where `bag` is insertion sort, so the multiset is a canonical sorted list; the interface makes `multiset` abstract so clients do not depend on that choice. The laws cover bounds under update, swap and slicing (`range_set`, `bag_swap`, `permutation_swap`), sortedness (`insert_sorted`, `sorted_glue`, `sorted_take`, `sorted_set`) and counting (`permutation_count`, `count_append`, `count_extensional`).

Nothing is trusted beyond `Vox_sequence`; all laws are proved by recursion. The module supplies `sorted` and `permutation` for [quicksort](demo:quicksort) and the rotation proof in `testsuite/tests/vox/collection_theory.ml`.

notes.title: Permutation is equality of bags
notes.text: `bag` sorts a list by repeated `insert`, so two lists are permutations exactly when their sorted forms are equal. With equality of complete values (`===`), a permutation is one equation between two terms, with no quantifier over elements.

notes.title: From equal counts to permutation
notes.text: Two sorted lists with equal counts of every integer are equal: compare heads, and if they differ the smaller one has count zero on the other side (`count_below`). `count_extensional` applies this to the bags, which are sorted by `bag_sorted`, so a client proves a permutation by proving equal counts pointwise.

what.short: The implementation behind the table's trusted storage interface: an abstract handle type, two ghost records and 17 external declarations, all assumed.
long: This file restates [`vox_table_storage.mli`](src:verification/library/vox_table_storage.mli) as an implementation. It declares the abstract handle type `t`, the ghost-only records `view` (a `Vox_table_model.state`) and `stored_key`, and 17 `external`s: `location`, `create`, `capacity`, `size`, `deleted`, `read_control`, `write_control`, `write_slot`, `write_value`, `clear_slot`, `set_counts`, `read_key`, `read_value`, `match16`, `match16_empty`, `clear` and `replace_storage`. There is no OCaml body and no proof in it.

Everything here is trusted: each external's refined type is its contract, and the checker assumes it at every call. The contracts state reads as observations of the ghost `Vox_table_model.state` held at `location table` in the caller's token, and writes as `H.put` of an updated state at that location. The C symbols are in `runtime/pref.c`; the natively inlined ones (`[@@builtin]`) are lowered in `backend/cmm_builtins.ml`.

The SIMD mask externals are `match16` and `match16_empty`, declared here and in the `.mli`. Their `runtime/pref.c` stubs pass the control-byte block to `caml_vox_control_match16` and `caml_vox_control_match16_empty` in `runtime/vox_control.c` (NEON, SSE2 or scalar), and `backend/cmm_builtins.ml` lowers them to inline vector code. The only other table external is `count_trailing_zeros` in [`vox_table_bits.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_bits.ml). Part of [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table)'s trusted base.

notes.title: The SIMD mask contracts

notes.title: Publishing rebuilt storage
notes.text: `replace_storage` consumes a token that owns exactly the temporary table (`H.put (H.empty ()) (location source) replacement.model`) and makes the destination's location hold `replacement.model`. Natively it is `caml_vox_table_exchange`, which swaps fields 2 to 5 of the two handles in `runtime/pref.c`, so the destination keeps its identity and `location`.

what.short: The ghost storage model: a record of capacity, counts, slots and control bytes, and the exact 16-lane mask function the SIMD contracts are stated with.
long: `state` is the table as the proofs see it: `capacity`, `size`, `deleted`, `slots : ('k * 'v) option list` and `controls : int list`, which has `capacity + 15` bytes so that a 16-byte load at any group offset below `capacity` stays in bounds. `initial` is the empty table (every control byte EMPTY, 128). `slot`, `control`, `set_slot`, `set_control` and `set_counts` are defined with `Vox_sequence.at`/`set`. `set_byte` writes a control byte and, for the first 15 indices, its clone at `capacity + index`; `remove_slot` clears a slot, writes the tombstone 254 and adjusts both counts. `lane_bit` and the recursive `matching` give the exact bit mask of lanes equal to a byte.

The file is checked OCaml: every function is a `[@def]` total definition that the verifier accepts. It is nonetheless part of what a reviewer must read to trust [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table), because the trusted storage and SIMD contracts in [`vox_table_storage.mli`](src:verification/library/vox_table_storage.mli) are stated in terms of it. Lemmas about it are in [`vox_table_model_proofs.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_model_proofs.ml).

notes.title: The model record
notes.text: Slots are `option`s, so an EMPTY slot and a tombstone both appear as `None`; only the control byte (128 or 254) tells them apart. The 15 extra control bytes are the wrapping clones of bytes 0 to 14.

notes.title: The exact lane mask
notes.text: `matching s offset byte lanes` sets bit `i` exactly when `control s (offset + i) = Some byte`, for `i < lanes`. The SIMD externals are specified with `lanes = 16`; [`vox_table_mask.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_mask.ml) proves the per-lane reading `Vox_table_mask.get` from this definition.

what.short: Lemmas about the storage model: reading after repeat and set, the initial state, control-byte writes with their clones, and tombstone removal.
long: Sequence facts (`repeat_at`, `repeat_length`, `at_set`, `set_negative`, `at_present`, `length_nonnegative`) and their consequences for `Vox_table_model.state`: `initial_slot`, `initial_control`, `slot_write`, `control_write`, `control_present`, `byte_write`, `byte_at`, `byte_at_primary` and `byte_clone` say what `set_byte` changes, including the clone byte, and `remove_fields` unfolds `remove_slot` into its slot, byte and count updates.
All lemmas are verified ghost code. They are used by the invariant proofs of [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table): initialization, insertion, removal and the read proofs.

notes.title: A byte write and its clone
notes.text: `byte_write` states the effect of `M.set_byte` on any control index: the written index and, when `index < 15`, its clone at `capacity + index` read `byte`; every other index is unchanged. The insertion and removal proofs use it to show that no new EMPTY byte appears.

what.short: Proves the per-lane meaning of the 16-lane mask: bit lane is set exactly when that lane's control byte equals the needle, and the mask fits in 16 bits.
long: `prefix`, `lane_bounds`, `prefix_step` and `distinct_lanes` are bit facts about `Vox_table_model.lane_bit`. `bounded` shows that `M.matching model offset needle count` has no bit at lane `count` or above and lies in `[0, 65535]`; `get` shows `(matching ... land lane_bit lane <> 0) = (control model (offset + lane) === Some needle)`.

Verified. In [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table) this is the bridge between the trusted mask contracts, which return `M.matching`, and the per-slot reasoning of the search and vacancy proofs (through `Vox_table_read_proofs.matching_control`).

notes.title: One lane of the mask
notes.text: Induction on `count`: the top lane is decided by the last step of `matching`, and a lower lane's bit is unaffected by `lor` with a different lane's bit (`distinct_lanes`).

what.short: Modular index arithmetic for power-of-two capacities: masking equals addmod, and shifts by 3, 4 and 7 stated arithmetically for use in specifications.
long: `wrap_add` proves `(value + delta) land (capacity - 1) = Vox_table_probe.addmod capacity value delta` for a power-of-two `capacity`; `wrap_range` bounds a masked index. `shifted` describes a logical right shift by `2^k` in arithmetic terms, and `lsr3`, `lsr4`, `lsr7` compute the shifts with `Int.Refined.( lsr )` and return that description, with `_spec` lemmas for predicates that mention them. `scale16`, `split16` and `scale_addmod` relate slot offsets to group numbers (multiples of 16).

Verified. It serves [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table)'s probe sequence and coverage proofs. The comments record why the shifts are functions: `( lsr )` is not total and a predicate cannot pass a constant to its refined count.

notes.title: The one slow query
notes.text: `wrap_add` is the only table proof marked `[@warning "-slow-refinement"]`: Z3 bit-blasts the 63-bit sum against a symbolic mask. The comment records that splitting it into lemmas did not make it cheaper.

notes.title: Shifts as arithmetic
notes.text: `shifted` is `[@def transparent]`, so its body is available wherever it is applied. It covers negative inputs too, since hashes may be any signed integer and `lsr` treats them as unsigned.

what.short: Triangular probing visits every group: triangle numbers modulo a power of two, a ghost plan of doublings, and an explicit inverse of the triangle map.
long: `triangle m r` is `0 + 1 + ... + r` computed with `addmod` modulo `m`. `plan = One | Twice of plan` is an inductive ghost value with `groups plan = 2^depth`, so a proof can induct on the number of doublings. `inverse plan offset` computes, by recursion on the plan, the rank at which the triangle sequence reaches `offset`; `inverse_at` proves `triangle (groups plan) (inverse plan offset) = offset` for every `offset < groups plan`, and `inverse_rank` proves the other composition. The step lemmas are `low_triangle` (the triangle sequence modulo `2n` reduces to the one modulo `n`) and `reflection` (rank `2n - 1 - r` lands on the flip of rank `r`).

Verified. This is the number theory behind [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table)'s claim that probing over groups of 16 reaches every slot within `capacity / 16` steps, used by [`vox_table_coverage.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_coverage.ml) and, through it, by the vacancy argument that insertion always finds a free slot.

notes.title: The ghost plan

notes.to: | Twice previous -> valid previous && groups previous <= 67108864
notes.text: The table carries a `plan` in its ghost view; `Vox_table_invariant.valid` requires `capacity = 16 * groups plan`. Growth replaces it with `Twice plan`, which is how the proofs know the capacity is a power of two built by doubling.

notes.title: Every group is reached
notes.text: `inverse` solves the triangle sequence for an offset by first solving it in the half-size table, then choosing between the rank found and its reflection. `inverse_at` proves this rank is in range and hits `offset`, so the triangle map is onto.

what.short: Proves that every slot lies on every key's probe sequence within capacity/16 ranks, by relating the probe recurrence to triangle numbers.
long: `probe_triangle` shows that `Vox_table_invariant.probe capacity hash rank` is the start group plus `16 * triangle groups rank`, modulo `capacity`, with step `16 * (rank + 1)`. `cover` then takes any slot index and returns a `(rank, lane)` with `rank < capacity / 16` and `lane < 16` such that the slot is lane `lane` of the group at `rank` on the probe sequence of `hash`; it uses `Vox_table_probe.inverse` for the rank. `empty_free_at` extracts one group's fact from `empty_free`. The top-level `addmod_associative` and `addmod_range` are arithmetic helpers.

Verified ghost code. In [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table) it is used only by [`vox_table_vacancy_progress.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_vacancy_progress.ml): if no group on a key's sequence had an EMPTY byte, then no slot at all would be EMPTY.

notes.title: The probe recurrence is a triangle sum
notes.text: Induction on `rank`. The step case needs `W.wrap_add` (masking equals `addmod`), `W.scale_addmod` (scaling by 16 commutes with `addmod`) and associativity of `addmod`.

notes.title: Coverage
notes.text: The distance from the key's start slot to `index` splits into a block number `distance lsr 4` and a lane `distance land 15`; the rank is the inverse of the block under the triangle map. The result is a ghost pair, returned as a witness.

what.short: A counting lemma: if no slot is EMPTY, live entries plus tombstones equal the capacity, which the load reserve rules out.
long: `occupied entry byte` says a slot is either live with a non-tombstone byte or `None` with byte 254. `full_count` proves by induction that when every index below `count` is occupied in this sense, `live_count slots + deleted_count controls count = count`. It takes the per-index fact as a higher-order ghost proof argument. `reserve_positive` and `not_full` are the arithmetic that turns `size + deleted <= capacity - capacity/8` into `size + deleted <> capacity`.
Verified. Part of the vacancy argument of [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table), used by [`vox_table_vacancy_progress.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_vacancy_progress.ml).

notes.title: Counting a full table
notes.text: The premise `(index : int) -> {u : unit | ...}` is a ghost function: a proof for every index. The recursive call passes a shifted proof `fun index -> proof (index + 1)`, the usual pattern for lemmas quantified over positions.

what.short: The representation invariant: the probe sequence, control-byte fingerprints, clone bytes, counts with a 1/8 reserve, distinct keys, and a ghost route per entry.
long: `Make (Key)` defines the internal `view`, three ghost fields: the storage `model`, a `routes` list with one `(depth, lane)` per slot, and the probe `plan`. `probe` is triangular probing in groups of 16 (start `(hash lsr 7) land (capacity - 1)`, step 16, 32, 48, ...), and `group` its group offsets. `empty_free s hash d` says none of the first `d` groups on the sequence contains an EMPTY byte. `route` says a live entry sits in lane `lane` of the group at `depth` on its own key's sequence and that every earlier group is EMPTY-free. `cells_valid` says a live slot's byte is `hash land 127` and an empty slot's is 128 or 254; `clones` says bytes `capacity + i` copy bytes `i < 15`; `shape` fixes a power-of-two capacity in `[16, 2^30]`, list lengths, the counts, and `size + deleted <= capacity - capacity lsr 3`.

`valid` is their conjunction together with `Map.distinct` of the slots and `routes_valid`. It is a `[@def]` ghost predicate and needs no trust; every operation of [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table) takes a view refined by `valid` and proves it of the view it returns. The public interface hides it: the facade's `view` type carries it as a refinement.

notes.title: Probe sequence and EMPTY-free prefixes
notes.text: The hash's high bits choose the first group and its low 7 bits are the fingerprint (`hash land 127`), SwissTable's h1/h2 split. `empty_free` is the fact that makes a search stop sound: a search that saw an EMPTY byte in some group could not have passed a stored equal key's group.

notes.title: Every entry lies on its probe path
notes.text: `routes` is a ghost witness, one path per slot, checked by `routes_valid`. It records the depth at which each entry was placed, which the probe invariant would otherwise have to existentially quantify.

notes.title: Shape and validity
notes.text: The 1/8 reserve (`reserve` is `capacity lsr 3`) guarantees at least one EMPTY byte, which the vacancy scan relies on. `valid` also ties the capacity to the ghost `plan` (`capacity = scale16 (groups plan)`), which gives the coverage proof an induction.

what.short: The key-law signature and the slot-list map: lookup, absence, distinctness and agreement modulo Key.equal, with lemmas for single-slot writes.
long: `module type Key` is the key interface used throughout: `equal` and `hash` at `@@ total`, and the laws `reflexive`, `symmetric`, `transitive` and `hash_equal` as total functions returning refined `unit`. `Make (Key)` reads a slot list `(Key.t * 'a) option list` as a map. `lookup`, `absent`, `distinct`, `agrees`, `same`, `erase` and `put` are `[@def]` definitions; the lemmas cover writes at one index (`insert_at`, `replace_at`, `remove_at`, `distinct_insert`, `distinct_remove`, `same_insert`, `same_remove`, `absent_set`), congruence under `Key.equal` (`lookup_congruent`, `erase_congruent`, `put_congruent`), and the extensionality lemmas `absent_intro`, `agrees_intro` and `same_intro`, which take a ghost proof for every index or query.

Verified. This is the middle of the three models of [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table): the storage model's `slots`, read as a map. The invariant requires `distinct` slots, and every mutation's internal contract is `Map.same` of the new slots with `Map.put` or `Map.erase` of the old.

notes.title: What a key must provide
notes.text: The laws are ordinary total functions, so a client proves them once, in Vox, and passes them with the key module. Hashes may collide and may be any integer; `hash_equal` is the only link between equality and hashing.

notes.title: Absence from a proof per index
notes.text: `absent_intro` concludes `absent slots query` from a ghost function proving, for each index, that the slot there does not hold a key equal to `query`. The search's stop proofs build this function from the probe invariant.

notes.title: Extensional sameness
notes.text: Two distinct slot lists with equal `lookup` at every query are `same`. The premise is a higher-order ghost proof; the update, insertion and migration proofs discharge their map equations through this lemma.

what.short: The public finite-map model: association lists with one binding per Key.equal class, and proofs of the seven laws the interface exports for Map.t.
long: `Make (Key).Assoc` defines association lists with `lookup`, `distinct`, `agrees`, `same`, `erase`, `put` and `count`, and proves their laws, including `same_count`: two distinct lists with the same bindings have the same length. The type `t = {entries : 'a Assoc.t | Assoc.distinct entries}` restricts them to distinct lists, and `lookup`, `put`, `erase`, `count` and `empty` lift the operations, with `put` and `erase` proving distinctness is preserved. The exported laws `lookup_empty`, `put_get`, `erase_get`, `count_put`, `count_erase`, `lookup_equal` and `count_nonnegative` are proved here.

Verified. [The flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table)'s interface makes `Map.t` abstract and exports only these operations and laws; this file is the model that shows they are consistent. The distinctness invariant is what makes `count` the number of bindings, so that a client can compute `length` after `replace` or `remove`.

notes.title: Counting is invariant under sameness
notes.text: Induction on `left`: erase its first key from both lists, which keeps them distinct and agreeing and shortens each by one. The facade uses this to show that the ghost map's count equals the live slot count, whatever the binding order.

notes.title: The public map type
notes.text: A refinement of the list type: the distinctness invariant lives in the type, so every `Map.t` a client can hold satisfies it, and the laws need not assume it.

what.short: Ghost compaction from the slot list to an association list, with proofs that it preserves lookup, distinctness, agreement, erase and put.
long: `compact` drops the `None` slots, turning the storage's slot list into an association list of `Vox_table_bindings`. `lookup`, `distinct`, `agrees`, `same`, `erase` and `put` are lemmas stating that `compact` commutes with the corresponding slot-map and association-list operations; `empty` shows that an all-empty slot list compacts to `[]`.

Verified ghost code. In [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table) the facade's `view` type requires `Assoc.same v.map (Bridge.compact v.storage.model.slots)`: this file is how facts proved about slots become facts about the public map.

notes.title: Compaction preserves lookup

notes.text: Physical holes, EMPTY or tombstone, disappear from the public model. The remaining lemmas have the same shape: unfold `compact` and the operation, then recurse on the tail.

what.short: Lemmas the reads rely on: per-slot facts from the invariant, clone bytes make wrapped 16-byte loads exact, and a matched lane holds a live entry.
long: `Make (Key)` instantiates `Vox_table_invariant.Make (Key)` as `I`. `cell_at` and `route_at` extract the invariant's per-slot conjuncts at an index. `clone_at` and `wrapped_control` show that the byte at `group + lane` equals the byte at the wrapped index, so a load that runs into the clone bytes sees the logically wrapped group; `matching_control` combines this with `Vox_table_mask.get`. `initialized` shows a lane that matches a fingerprint (at most 127) holds a live slot, which is the precondition of the trusted `read_key`. `route_info`, `route_equal_key` (an equal key has the same probe sequence, from `Key.hash_equal`), `slot_at`, `stored_control`, `group_range`, `group_in_shape`, `capacity_bounds` and `next_probe` are the remaining steps.
Verified. It is the base layer of [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table)'s search proofs and is reused by the vacancy scan and migration.

notes.title: Wrapped loads read the clones
notes.text: When `group + lane >= capacity`, the physical index lands in the 15 clone bytes, and `clone_at` equates it with the byte at `group + lane - capacity`. This is what lets `match16` read 16 contiguous bytes at any group offset.

notes.title: A matched lane is a live slot
notes.text: EMPTY (128) and DELETED (254) are above 127, so a lane whose byte equals a fingerprint cannot be a hole. `Vox_table_search.candidates` uses this to meet `read_key`'s precondition.

what.short: The facts a partial search carries: the candidates of a mask miss the query, and every group so far on its probe sequence was searched.
long: `misses model query index` says the slot at `index` does not hold a key equal to `query`. `candidates_absent model query group mask` walks the mask in the order the search does (`Vox_table_bits.first`, then `clear`) and requires every candidate to miss. `prefix_absent model query count` says this holds for the fingerprint mask of each of the first `count` groups on the query's probe sequence. `candidate_at`, `prefix_at` and `empty_free_at` extract single instances.

Verified ghost definitions and lemmas. They are the loop invariants of `Vox_table_search.candidates` and `groups` in [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table), consumed by [`vox_table_stop_proof.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_stop_proof.ml).

notes.title: Candidates that missed

notes.text: The definition follows the runtime loop exactly, lowest lane first, so the search's postcondition is stated in the same terms as its code. It decreases on the mask, since `clear` removes a set bit.

notes.title: Groups already searched
notes.text: `groups` in the search carries `prefix_absent view.model query rank` in its token's refinement and extends it by one group per iteration.

what.short: Lookup code: the SIMD group scan along the probe sequence and the candidate loop, with contracts that return an equal key's slot or prove the key absent.
long: `candidates` walks a fingerprint mask with `Vox_table_bits.first` and `clear`, reading each candidate key with the trusted `read_key`, and returns its index when `Key.equal` holds, or -1 with `candidates_absent`. `groups` scans the probe sequence: one `match16_empty` per group gives the fingerprint mask and an EMPTY flag; after the candidates miss, an EMPTY lane ends the search (`Proof.empty_stop`), and otherwise it moves to the next group. The rank bound `capacity lsr 4` ends it with `Proof.exhausted`. `find_index_hashed` handles a 16-slot table with a single `match16` and otherwise calls `groups`; `find_index` hashes the key; `find_opt` reads the value and returns `I.Map.lookup view.model.slots query`.

Verified. This is the executable read path of [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table), used by `find_opt`, `find`, `mem`, `replace` and `remove`. Its correctness rests on the trusted storage and SIMD contracts and on the stop proofs in [`vox_table_stop_proof.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_stop_proof.ml). `groups` is `[@inline never]` so that the key comparisons inline into it when the functor is specialized.

notes.title: The candidate loop's contract
notes.text: The mask is refined to a subset of `M.matching view.model group needle 16`. The result is either an index holding a key `Key.equal` to the query or -1 with `Spec.candidates_absent`, which the group loop accumulates into `prefix_absent`.
