notes.text: `scanned land 65535` is the fingerprint mask and `scanned land 65536` the EMPTY flag, both from one `match16_empty`. The two `-1` returns are justified by `Proof.exhausted` and `Proof.empty_stop`; `R.next_probe` keeps the token's refinement `I.probe ... rank === (group, step)` in step with the runtime `group` and `step`.

what.short: Why a search may stop: a group with an EMPTY byte, or a full scan of capacity/16 groups, proves the query absent from the table.
long: `fingerprinted_misses` shows that a lane whose byte equals the query's fingerprint was among the candidates and therefore missed. `visited_misses` shows that an entry whose route lies at a searched rank cannot hold a key equal to the query: an equal key has the same hash, hence the same probe sequence and fingerprint. `stored_misses` handles any stored entry when the search stopped at a group with an EMPTY byte: if its route were deeper than the stop rank, the route's `empty_free` would contradict that EMPTY byte. `empty_stop` and `exhausted` assemble these with `Map.absent_intro` into `Map.absent` and `Map.lookup ... === None`.

Verified ghost code. This is the core correctness argument of [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table)'s lookup, the proof that open addressing with EMPTY-terminated probing is sound given the invariant in [`vox_table_invariant.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_invariant.ml).

notes.title: The EMPTY-stop argument
notes.text: Assume a stored key equal to the query. Its route gives a rank on the query's sequence. If the rank is at most the stop rank, `visited_misses` shows the search already compared it; otherwise `Spec.empty_free_at` says the stop group has no EMPTY byte, contradicting the search's observation.

notes.title: A full scan
notes.text: Every route has rank below `capacity / 16`, so once the search has visited that many groups every stored entry has been compared. The per-index proof passed to `Map.absent_intro` is a ghost closure over the stored entry.

what.short: Table creation, clearing, removal and value overwrite, each a sequence of trusted storage writes followed by a proof that the invariant and map equation hold.
long: `create` and `create_capacity` allocate with `T.create` and prove the initial view valid (with an all-`(0, 0)` routes list). `clear` calls the trusted bulk `T.clear`. `write_byte` writes a control byte and, for the first 15 indices, its clone. `erase_existing` clears a slot, writes the tombstone 254 and updates the counts, then calls `Proof.remove_valid`; `remove` searches with `find_index` and either returns the view unchanged (proving `same` with `erase` of an absent key) or erases the found slot and bridges from the stored key to the query. `write_existing` overwrites a value through `T.write_value`, keeping the stored key, and calls `Proof.replace_value`.

Verified; the only trusted steps are the storage externals it calls. Every function returns a new ghost view and a token whose heap is `H.put` of the old one at `T.location table`, which [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table)'s facade turns into its exact frame condition. Proofs are in [`vox_table_update_proofs.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_update_proofs.ml) and [`vox_table_initial.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_initial.ml).

notes.title: A control byte and its clone
notes.text: Two trusted `write_control` calls, whose composed effect is `M.set_byte`. `H.put_law` collapses the two heap updates at the same location into one.

notes.title: Removal
notes.text: The stored key may differ from `query` while being `Key.equal` to it; `erase_congruent` shows erasing either gives the same map. The ghost `key` and `value` are extracted with `unreachable_ ()` on the impossible branch, which the verifier proves unreachable.

what.short: Invariant proofs for overwriting a value and for tombstone removal: unchanged keys keep validity, and writes that add no EMPTY byte keep every route.
long: Two families of lemmas. For value replacement: `same_keys` says two slot lists hold the same keys at the same positions, and `valid_same_keys` shows `Invariant.valid` is then unchanged when counts, controls, routes and plan are equal; `replace_value` combines it with `Map.replace_at` and `same_intro` to get `Map.same after (Map.put before key value)`. For writes to control bytes: `matching_zero_preserved`, `empty_free_preserved`, `route_preserved` and `routes_preserved` show that if no index becomes EMPTY, every route stays valid; `clones_byte` keeps the clone bytes in sync; `remove_reachability`, `remove_shape` and `remove_valid` prove that writing the tombstone keeps the invariant and gives `Map.same after (Map.erase before key)`.

Verified ghost code. Used by [`vox_table_mutation.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_mutation.ml) and, for the route lemmas, by [`vox_table_insert_proofs.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_insert_proofs.ml) in [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table).

notes.title: Same keys, same validity
notes.text: Overwriting a value touches no control byte, count or key, so every conjunct of `valid` transfers. The proof goes conjunct by conjunct: shape, cells, routes, clones and distinctness.

notes.title: No new EMPTY byte keeps routes
notes.text: The premise is a ghost function saying any byte that is EMPTY after the write was EMPTY before. Insertion (a fingerprint byte) and removal (a tombstone) both satisfy it, so neither can invalidate another entry's route.

notes.title: Removal keeps the invariant
notes.text: The removed slot's byte is its key's fingerprint, which is not 254, so the tombstone increments `deleted` by exactly one. Routes are unchanged: the removed slot's route is still valid because a `None` entry trivially satisfies `route`.

what.short: Proves the freshly allocated or cleared table valid: all slots empty, all control bytes EMPTY, zero counts and trivial routes.
long: `empty_distinct`, `empty_count`, `no_deleted`, `shape`, `clones`, `cells` and `routes` prove each conjunct of `Vox_table_invariant.valid` for `Vox_table_model.initial capacity None` with routes `repeat capacity (0, 0)`. `initial` combines them for any power-of-two capacity in `[16, 2^30]` whose ghost plan matches.
Verified ghost code, used by `create`, `create_capacity` and `clear` in [`vox_table_mutation.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_mutation.ml) for [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table).

notes.title: The initial view is valid
notes.text: `entry` is a ghost `None` obtained from `Mutation.empty_entry`, so the lemma is stated for the same instance the allocation contract mentions.

what.short: Insertion of an absent key: find a vacant slot, check the load limit, and write slot, fingerprint byte and counts with a proof of the new invariant.
long: `write_new_hashed` writes the key and value with `T.write_slot`, the fingerprint `hash land 127` with `Mutation.write_byte`, and the counts with `T.set_counts` (a reused tombstone leaves `size + deleted` unchanged), then proves the resulting view valid and `Map.same` with `Map.put` through `Proof.insert_valid`. It records the vacancy's route `path` in the ghost `routes`. `try_insert_hashed` asks `Vacancy.find_hashed` for the first slot on the key's probe sequence with a DELETED or EMPTY byte, returns `inserted = false` with the table unchanged if the write would break the 1/8 reserve, and otherwise calls `write_new_hashed`.

Verified; the storage writes are trusted externals. In [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table) `try_insert_hashed` is called by `Vox_table_implementation.insert_absent_hashed`, which rebuilds and retries on failure, and by the migration copy loop.

notes.title: Three writes and one proof
notes.to: Proof.insert_valid before index key value old_byte path view);
notes.text: Each write consumes the token and returns one whose heap has an updated model at `T.location table`; `H.put_law` composes the three updates. The new view's `model` is `Proof.insert_model`, the model-level description of the same writes.

notes.title: The load check
notes.text: The result's refinement distinguishes the two outcomes: on `inserted = false` the view and heap are exactly the input's, so the caller can rebuild from the same state.

what.short: Invariant proof for inserting an absent key at a vacant slot on its probe path: fields, counts, cells, clones, routes, distinctness and the map equation.
long: `insert_model` is the model after insertion: `set_slot`, then `set_byte` with the fingerprint, then `set_counts` with `size + 1` and `deleted` reduced by one if the slot was a tombstone. `fields`, `shape`, `deleted_count`, `arithmetic` and `reserve_bounds` prove the shape conjunct, including the reserve; `cells_set` and `routes_set` update the per-slot invariants at the written index; `reachability` proves cells, clones and routes of the new view. `insert_valid` puts these together with `Map.distinct_insert` and `Map.same_insert`.

Verified ghost code, called from `Vox_table_insert.write_new_hashed` in [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table). It reuses the route-preservation lemmas of [`vox_table_update_proofs.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_update_proofs.ml).

notes.title: Other routes survive the insertion
notes.text: `no_new_empty` is a local ghost function: the written byte is a fingerprint at most 127, so no index becomes EMPTY. Passing it to `Update.route_preserved` carries the new entry's route, found by the vacancy scan in the old model, over to the new model; `routes_set` does the same for every other slot's route.

notes.title: The insertion theorem
notes.text: The premises are exactly what `Vox_table_insert.write_new_hashed` holds: a valid view, a vacant slot with its old byte, an absent key, room under the reserve, and a route to that slot. The conclusion is validity of the new view and `Map.same` with `Map.put`.

what.short: The vacancy scan for insertion: walk the key's probe sequence to the first group with a DELETED or EMPTY byte, returning the slot and its ghost route.
long: `scan` tests each group with two `match16` calls (bytes 254 and 128), prefers a tombstone, and picks the lowest matching lane with `Vox_table_bits.first`. Its result `found` is an unboxed record of the index, the byte and a ghost `path`, refined to say the slot is vacant, its byte is 128 or 254, and `I.route` holds for the query at that path. `vacant` and `route_here` are the lemmas for these facts; `find_hashed` starts the scan at rank 0.

Verified. The rank is a ghost argument bounded by `capacity / 16`; `Progress.not_exhausted` shows the bound is never reached, so the runtime loop needs no rank counter or exhaustion check, and every recursive call is proved within the bound. Part of insertion in [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table).

notes.title: The scan's contract
notes.text: `value` and `rank` are `@ ghost`: the runtime loop does no rank arithmetic and no bound check, and the rank survives only as an unused placeholder argument. The route in the result is what lets insertion extend `routes_valid` with the new entry.

notes.title: One group per step
notes.text: When the group has no vacancy it has no EMPTY byte, which extends `empty_free` by one rank; this is the fact the new entry's route needs, since every group before its slot must be EMPTY-free.

what.short: Proves that a valid table always has an EMPTY byte on every key's probe sequence within capacity/16 groups, so the vacancy scan cannot run out.
long: `full_scan` uses `Vox_table_coverage.cover` to show that if all `capacity / 16` groups on a key's sequence were EMPTY-free, no slot in the table would be EMPTY. `occupied_at` turns a non-EMPTY byte into the `occupied` predicate of [`vox_table_occupancy.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_occupancy.ml). `not_exhausted` then counts: all slots occupied gives `size + deleted = capacity` (`Count.full_count`), which contradicts the 1/8 reserve in `Vox_table_invariant.shape`.

Verified ghost code. It is the termination-shaped fact of [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table)'s insertion: the scan in [`vox_table_vacancy.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_vacancy.ml) calls `not_exhausted` at each step to justify its ghost rank bound.

notes.title: The scan is never exhausted
notes.text: Three steps: coverage (every slot is on the sequence), occupancy (every slot is live or a tombstone), and counting against the reserve. The per-index proof passed to `full_count` is a ghost closure.

what.short: The rebuild copy loop: insert every live entry of the old storage into a fresh table, maintaining that the copy has the same bindings as a prefix of the source.
long: `copy_loop` walks source indices `0 .. capacity - 1`. It reads each control byte with the trusted `read_control`; for 128 or 254 it skips the slot, and otherwise it reads the key and value and calls `Insert.try_insert` on the destination, which may fail when the destination is too small. The loop invariant, in the destination token's refinement, is `I.Map.same before.model.slots (S.take index source_view.model.slots)`, together with a frame `P.own t === H.put heap (T.location destination) ...`. `classify` relates a byte to the slot's contents; `copy` fixes the frame heap and starts the loop.

Verified. It borrows the source token read-only and owns the destination token. On completion `Vox_table_resize.rebuild_into` publishes the destination's storage. Part of rebuilding in [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table); the map lemmas are in [`vox_table_migration_proofs.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_migration_proofs.ml).

notes.title: The copy invariant
notes.to: @ unique = fun source source_view destination before index heap
notes.text: The destination's slots are `same` as the first `index` source slots. At `index = capacity` this is `same` with the whole source, which `S.take_all` provides; on an early `complete = false` only validity and the frame are promised.

notes.title: Skip or copy
notes.text: `Proof.destination_absent` shows the key is not yet in the destination, which `try_insert` requires: source keys are distinct, so a key cannot occur in the prefix already copied.

what.short: Map lemmas for the rebuild loop: prefixes of a distinct slot list stay distinct, a later key is absent from the prefix, and copy and skip steps extend the prefix.
long: `take_absent`, `take_distinct`, `prefix_absent` and `prefix_next` are facts about `Vox_sequence.take` of a slot list under `Vox_table_map`. `destination_absent` shows that the key at source index `i` is absent from a destination `same` as the first `i` slots. `copy_step` and `skip_step` extend the loop invariant by one slot, for a copied entry and for a hole; `empty_start` proves it at index 0 for a fresh table.

Verified ghost code, used by [`vox_table_migrate.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_migrate.ml) and [`vox_table_resize.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_table_resize.ml) in [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table).

notes.title: One copy step
notes.text: After inserting the entry at `index`, the destination is `same` as the prefix of length `index + 1`. The proof is extensional: `same_intro` with a ghost proof comparing `lookup` at every query.

what.short: Rebuilding: choose the new capacity, copy into fresh storage, double again if the copy fails, and publish the result into the original handle.
long: `rebuild` rebuilds at the same capacity when at least 1/8 of the slots are tombstones and at double capacity otherwise. `rebuild_into` allocates a fresh table with `Mutation.create_capacity` from a token that owns nothing (`P.empty ()`), runs `Migrate.copy`, and on success calls the trusted `T.replace_storage` to move the fresh storage into the original handle, so its `location` and identity are kept. If the copy fails it doubles again with `Probe.Twice plan`. Above 2^29 slots it raises `Invalid_argument "Vox_verified_flat_hashtbl: capacity exhausted"`. `double_capacity` and `double_plan` prove the new capacity is a power of two at most 2^30 matching the new ghost plan.

Verified, apart from the trusted storage externals. The contract is `I.valid` of the result, `I.Map.same` of old and new slots, and the heap frame. Termination of the doubling recursion is not claimed; the capacity bound ends it. Part of [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table)'s insertion path.

notes.title: Copy, publish or grow
notes.to: rebuild_into table before next_capacity next_plan token
notes.text: The fresh table's token owns exactly `H.put (H.empty ()) (location fresh.table) ...`, which is the precondition of `replace_storage`; that trusted call consumes it. The ghost `plan` is the only per-capacity proof state that changes when doubling.

what.short: The internal table driver: create, lookups, length, remove, clear, and replace, which overwrites an equal key's value or inserts, rebuilding until there is room.
long: `Make (Key)` re-exports `create`, `find_opt`, `remove` and `clear` from the lower modules and defines `length`, `find` (raises `Not_found` for an absent key), `mem`, `insert_absent_hashed` and `replace`. `replace` searches once with `find_index_hashed`; on a hit it overwrites the value with `Mutation.write_existing`, keeping the stored key, and on a miss it calls `insert_absent_hashed`, which tries `Insert.try_insert_hashed` and, on failure, calls `Resize.rebuild` and retries without searching again. The local `Proof` module holds `lookup_found`, `absent_after_rebuild`, `put_after_rebuild` and `put_equal_key`.

Verified. Its contracts are stated on the internal slot model (`I.Map.same ... (I.Map.put ...)`, `I.valid`); [`vox_verified_flat_hashtbl.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_verified_flat_hashtbl.ml) bridges them to the public `Map.t`. Only normal return is specified; the retry recursion has no termination proof. This is the top of [the flat hash table](demo:flat-hash-table)'s internal module stack.

notes.title: Insert, rebuild, retry
notes.text: A failed attempt returns the unchanged view and token, so the rebuild starts from the original state. After the rebuild the key is still absent (`absent_after_rebuild`), and `put_after_rebuild` composes `same rebuilt before` with the inserted map.

notes.title: Replace with an equal key
notes.to: ghost_ (Proof.put_equal_key before result.#view stored key value);
notes.text: The slot keeps the stored key, which is `Key.equal` to `key` but may be a different value; `put_equal_key` uses `Map.put_congruent` to show that `put stored value` and `put key value` are the same map.

what.short: The top of the LZ4 specification: the error types and the two relations the public contracts use, matches_model for decoding and compresses for compression.
long: The entry point of the [LZ4](demo:lz4) specification and the first of the ten files a reviewer must read to know what `Vox_lz4`'s contracts mean. It defines the public error types (`malformed`, `decode_error` with `Malformed`, `Output_limit`, `Invalid_capacity`), the result type `decoded`, and two `let[@def]` relations, each of which also yields a `_def` equation lemma for proofs.

`matches_model wire capacity result` uses `Vox_lz4_spec_decode_bytes.decode_block` on the wire's contents and requires the capacity to lie in 0 to 4,194,304, the result's error kind to equal the model's status, and on `Ok output` the string length to equal the model's count and every byte to agree via `matches_bytes`. The `malformed` reason and position are left unconstrained. `compresses source wire` is false above 4,194,304 source bytes and otherwise says that the wire is exactly the layout (`Vox_lz4_spec_wire.wire_matches_plan`) of the plan chosen by `Vox_lz4_spec_scan.from_source`.

Both relations are ghost definitions: the verifier checks that they are total and well typed, and their meaning is what the reviewer accepts as the definition of LZ4 here. [vox_lz4.mli](src:verification/library/vox_lz4.mli) states its contracts in terms of these two relations.

notes.title: The decoder relation
notes.text: The public decoder contract. Only the error kind is compared with the model, so `Malformed`'s reason and position are unspecified; `Invalid_capacity` never satisfies the relation, and a successful result must have the model's length and bytes.

notes.title: The compression relation
notes.text: Compression is specified as byte identity with the wire layout of one plan, the compressor model's `from_source`. Any other valid encoding of the source fails this relation.

what.short: LZ4 specification: bytes, the trusted char/byte conversions, token nibbles, extended-length reading and the decoder's three statuses.
long: Part of the ten-file [LZ4](demo:lz4) specification. It defines the refined type `byte` (0 to 255), `high4` and `low15` (the token's two nibbles, with refinements relating them to the token value), `read_extended_length` and `read_length` (the LZ4 length encoding: a nibble of 15 is followed by bytes that are added until one is not 255), the `length_result` type (`Length`, `Length_truncated`, `Length_limit`) and the decoder status `Done | Malformed | Output_limit`.

`char_of_byte` and `byte_of_char` are trusted: both are `external ... = "%identity"` declared total, and `byte_of_char`'s result carries the assumed contract `char_of_byte byte === c`. Everything else is checked. `read_extended_length` reports `Length_limit` as soon as the accumulated length would exceed 4,194,304, which is how an oversized length becomes an output-limit error in the decoder model.

notes.title: Trusted byte conversions
notes.text: The two `%identity` externals are the specification's byte assumption: every `char` is some `byte` whose `char_of_byte` gives it back. The converse law is stated separately by a second `char_of_byte` in `vox_lz4_snapshot.ml`.

notes.title: Extended lengths
notes.text: Reads 255-valued extension bytes until a smaller one ends the length. Running out of input is `Length_truncated` (malformed); exceeding 4,194,304 is `Length_limit` (output limit). The fuel argument only serves termination; `read_length` passes the remaining input length.

what.short: LZ4 specification: the decoder model, a total function giving status, byte count and the decoded bytes (in reverse) for every input block and capacity.
long: The decoder half of the [LZ4](demo:lz4) specification, and the file `Vox_lz4_spec.matches_model` calls. `decode_block` fixes the initial decoder state; its worker `decode_model` walks the block one sequence at a time and returns a `model_result` of `kind`, `count` and the ghost list `reversed` of output bytes, most recent first. Helpers: `at_distance` (the byte `distance` positions back), `copy_bytes` (a match copy, one byte at a time, so overlapping copies read bytes they just wrote), `literal_bytes`, and `matches_bytes`, which compares a reversed byte list with the first `count` elements of an array.

Every decision of a decoder is fixed here: an empty or exhausted input is `Malformed`; a length past 4,194,304 or a literal or match run that does not fit the capacity is `Output_limit`; a truncated length, literal run or offset, a zero offset or one reaching before the output start is `Malformed`. The last sequence must have a zero low nibble and, if the block has a match, at least five literals and a last match that starts at least 12 bytes before the end. These are ghost definitions checked for totality; the reviewer accepts them as the meaning of decoding.

The implementation is proved against the heap model in [vox_lz4_spec_decode.ml](src:verification/library/vox_lz4_spec_decode.ml), which has the same control structure; `Vox_lz4_decode_bytes_proof` relates the two models.

notes.title: Final-sequence rules
notes.text: A sequence whose literals reach the end of the input ends the block. It is rejected as malformed if its token has a match nibble, or, after any match, if it has fewer than five literals or the last match started within 12 bytes of the end (LZ4's LASTLITERALS and MFLIMIT rules).

notes.title: Offset, match length and the recursive step
notes.text: The two offset bytes are little-endian; offset 0 or an offset past the bytes decoded so far is malformed. A match length that does not fit the capacity is an output-limit error, checked before any byte of the sequence is appended. The recursive call records the match start as `last_match_start` for the final-sequence check.

notes.title: Observation of the output
notes.text: Relates the reversed model list to an output array: the list's head is element `count - 1`, and the list has exactly `count` elements.

what.short: LZ4 specification: bounded source access, source-distance equality, length extensions, literal tokens and per-byte wire predicates.
long: Part of the ten-file [LZ4](demo:lz4) specification, used by the wire layout in `vox_lz4_spec_wire.ml`. It defines `source_at` (an `option`-valued bounded read), `literal_token` (the token of a final literal run), `extension_count` (how many length-extension bytes a remaining length needs: one per full 255, plus a final byte), `extension_bytes` (the wire holds 255s and then the remainder), `literal_bytes` (the wire copies a range of the source) and `wire_byte` (the wire holds a given byte at a position). `source_matches_distance source index distance n` compares the source observations at `index + k` and `index + k - distance` for each of the next `n` positions.

`same_char` is trusted: an `external ... = "%eq"` declared total whose contract says it returns `left === right`. The other definitions are checked; the `extension_count` refinement bounds are proved.

notes.title: Trusted character equality
notes.text: `same_char` is the one assumption in this file: physical equality on `char` is taken to decide logical equality. The match search in `vox_lz4_spec_match.ml` compares bytes with it.

notes.title: Length extension bytes
notes.text: A remaining length of 255 or more emits a 255 byte and continues; a smaller one emits itself and stops. So an exact multiple of 255 ends with a zero byte, as LZ4 requires, and `extension_count` is the count of bytes `extension_bytes` describes.

what.short: LZ4 specification: wire_matches_plan, the exact byte layout of a plan's sequences and final literal run, including the total wire length.
long: Part of the ten-file [LZ4](demo:lz4) specification. `wire_matches_plan source wire anchor cursor plan` says that from `cursor` on the wire holds, for each `Sequence`, a token (`match_token`), literal-length extensions, the literals copied from `source`, a two-byte little-endian offset (`split_distance`) and match-length extensions, followed by the rest of the plan; and for `End`, a `literal_token`, extensions and the remaining literals, ending exactly at the end of the wire. `extra_count` is the number of extension bytes for a length (0 below 15).

The relation also requires a valid plan, a source of at most 4,194,304 bytes and a wire of at most 4,210,768 bytes (4,194,304 plus the 16,449 extension bytes that length needs plus 15). Because both cases pin every position and the `End` case fixes the length, at most one wire satisfies it for a given source and plan, which is what makes `Vox_lz4_spec.compresses` a byte-identity contract. It is a ghost definition checked for totality.

notes.title: The final literal run
notes.text: The last run is a token, its extensions and the remaining source bytes, and the wire must end right after them: no trailing bytes are allowed.

notes.title: One sequence on the wire
notes.text: The layout is token, literal extensions, literals, offset low byte, offset high byte, match extensions. The match nibble encodes `length - 4`. `next_cursor < Iarray.length wire` requires at least one more byte, so a sequence is never the last thing on the wire.

what.short: LZ4 specification: the sequence token byte built from literal and match lengths, and the split of an offset into low and high bytes.
long: Part of the ten-file [LZ4](demo:lz4) specification, used by `vox_lz4_spec_wire.ml`. `match_token literals match_code` is `16 * min literals 15 + min match_code 15`, stated as its refinement. `split_distance` returns a `distance_bytes` record `{low; high}` with `distance = low + 256 * high`, computed by eight conditional subtractions of 32768 down to 256, with no division.

Both functions are total and checked, and their refinements are proved; as part of the specification, their meaning is what a reviewer reads. The streaming compressor computes the offset split with integer division and proves it equal to this one.

notes.title: Offset split
notes.text: The refinement `distance = r.low + 256 * r.high`, together with the `byte` type of both fields, determines the pair uniquely, so this is the little-endian encoding of the offset.

what.short: LZ4 specification: a plan is a list of matches (position, distance, length), and valid_plan states LZ4's constraints on each match.
long: Part of the ten-file [LZ4](demo:lz4) specification. `sequence` is a record `{position; distance; length}`, and `plan` is `End | Sequence of sequence * plan` (`[@@inductive]`, so the verifier can reason about it by structure). Literal runs are implicit: the literals of a sequence are the source bytes from the previous match's end (the `anchor`) to its `position`.

`valid_plan source anchor plan` requires, for each match, that it starts at or after the anchor and at most 12 bytes before the end, that its distance is 1 to 65,535 and reaches no earlier than the source start, that its length is at least 4 and leaves the last five bytes as literals, and that the source bytes really repeat at that distance (`Vox_lz4_spec_bytes.source_matches_distance`). It is a ghost definition checked for totality.

notes.title: Validity of a plan
notes.text: These conditions are the encoder-side counterparts of the decoder model's rules: a 16-bit offset, a minimum match of 4, the 12-byte last-match rule and five final literals. `source_matches_distance` makes each match correct as a copy.

what.short: LZ4 specification: maximal match search, candidate validation and the four-byte multiplicative hash.
long: Part of the ten-file [LZ4](demo:lz4) specification; it fixes how the compressor model hashes and matches. The source-distance equality predicate is defined in [`vox_lz4_spec_bytes.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_lz4_spec_bytes.ml). `scan_match` and `match_length` extend a match byte by byte up to a limit and return the maximal length. `choose_match source position limit hint` treats `hint` as a candidate earlier position: it returns `None` if the hint is negative, at or after `position`, more than 65,535 back, or if fewer than 4 bytes match, and otherwise the distance and maximal length. `hash_bytes` packs four bytes little-endian into an `int32`, multiplies by `0x9e3779b1l`, shifts right by 16 and returns the result, so hashes are 16-bit; `hash4` applies it at a position.

Trusted: the six `int32` externals (`int32_of_int`, `int32_to_int`, `int32_or`, `int32_mul`, `int32_lsl`, `int32_lsr`) are declared total with no contract, so nothing is proved about the values they compute; `hash_bytes` therefore falls back to 0 if the result is outside 0 to 65,535, which keeps its refinement provable, and `choose_match` checks every match against the source bytes, whatever the hash. The rest is checked. The scanner calls the checked extension lemma in [`vox_lz4_match_proof.ml`](src:verification/library/vox_lz4_match_proof.ml) only in ghost code.

notes.title: Candidate validation
notes.text: The hash table lookup supplies `hint`, but the result's refinement is proved from the source bytes alone. This is why the general round-trip theorem holds for arbitrary hints, and so for any hash function.

notes.title: The hash
notes.to: if 0 <= hash && hash < 65536 then hash else 0
notes.text: A Fibonacci-style multiplicative hash of the little-endian 32-bit word, keeping the top 16 bits. The final range check never changes the value at run time; it exists because the `int32` primitives carry no contract.

what.short: Proof that a matching source run extends by one equal byte, used by the LZ4 model and executable scanner.
what.long: `source_matches_distance_extend` is a ghost induction over the existing match length. Its contract uses the source-distance equality predicate from `Vox_lz4_spec_bytes`; it contributes no model definition or scanner choice.

notes.title: Extending a matching run
notes.text: The source-distance equality predicate is defined in `Vox_lz4_spec_bytes`. This lemma proves that a matching run extends by one byte when the next source bytes agree; its body is ghost code, checked for its contract and termination.

what.short: LZ4 specification: the compressor model's hash table as an association list, where lookup returns the most recent position for a hash or -1.
long: The smallest of the ten [LZ4](demo:lz4) specification files. `hashes` is `(int * int) list` of (hash, position) pairs, and `lookup hash entries` returns the position of the first pair with that hash, or -1. `Vox_lz4_spec_scan.scan` prepends each visited position, so the first pair is the most recent one: this is the immutable model of a table that overwrites its slot.

It is a checked total definition. The streaming compressor keeps a mutable 65,536-entry integer table and proves it agrees with this list at every step. `Vox_lz4_fast_plan_model` re-exports it by `include`.

notes.title: Most-recent lookup
notes.to: if key = hash then position else lookup hash rest
notes.text: Absent hashes give -1, which `choose_match` rejects as a candidate.

what.short: LZ4 specification: the compressor model, a total scan that fixes which positions are hashed, which candidate is tried and where matches go.
long: The compressor half of the [LZ4](demo:lz4) specification; `Vox_lz4_spec.compresses` lays out the plan that `from_source` returns. `scan source entries position anchor fuel` stops with `End` once `position` is more than 12 bytes from the end; otherwise it hashes the four bytes at `position` (`hash4`), looks up the previous position with that hash, records the current one, and asks `choose_match` for a match whose length leaves five final literals. On a miss it advances by one byte; on a match it emits a `Sequence` and resumes after the match. Positions inside a match are not hashed, and there is no step acceleration on long runs of misses.

The result type `{r | valid_plan source anchor r}` is proved, so the plan is valid by construction; `fuel` equals the remaining length plus one and justifies termination. This is a checked total definition whose behavior the reviewer accepts as the compression algorithm; `vox_lz4_forward_model.ml` re-exports it under the name the streaming proof uses.

notes.title: The scanner
notes.text: Each visited position is prepended to `entries` before matching, and only visited positions are recorded. A match jumps to `position + choice.length`, which becomes the next anchor, so the next sequence's literals start there.

what.short: The LZ4 decoder model over a ghost raw-memory heap: same decisions as the pure decoder model, with output written into heap cells.
long: An internal model for the [LZ4](demo:lz4) decoder proofs, outside the ten-file specification. It re-exports `Vox_lz4_spec_parse` and defines `copy_heap` and `literal_heap` (writes into `Raw_memory` locations of a ghost `Ghost_pref.heap`) and a `decode_model` whose control structure and statuses are the same as `Vox_lz4_spec_decode_bytes.decode_model`, with the output kept as a heap `state` in place of a reversed byte list.

It is checked ghost code. The mutable decoder in `vox_lz4_string_decode.ml` is proved against it (through `Vox_lz4_packed`, which includes it), and the lemmas `decode` and `observations` of `Vox_lz4_decode_bytes_proof` prove that this model and the pure one give the same status, count and output bytes, which carries the result to the public relation `matches_model`. The heap-level round-trip lemmas in `vox_lz4_general_wire.ml` are also stated against this model.

notes.title: Overlapping copy into the heap
notes.text: Each byte is read from `used - distance` after the previous byte has been written, so a distance shorter than the length repeats a pattern, as LZ4 decoders do. An uninitialized source cell stops the copy.

what.short: The predicate initialized, which says the first count cells of a raw LZ4 buffer hold a byte in a ghost heap; the assumed final-copy contract uses it.
long: A single ghost definition for the [LZ4](demo:lz4) executable boundary. `initialized h p count` holds when every location of raw buffer `p` below `count` maps to `Some (Some _)` in heap `h`, that is, has been written.

It is a checked total definition, and it gives meaning to trusted contracts: `vox_lz4_review_boundary.md` names it, with `vox_lz4_heap_bytes.ml`, as the storage predicates behind `Vox_lz4_string_copy.copy_prefix`'s assumed contract. The buffer and snapshot modules use it too. It is not part of the ten-file semantic specification.

what.short: An early, standalone LZ4 sequence model over byte lists with overlapping copy and a checked-match lemma; used only by tests.
long: A small model predating the current [LZ4](demo:lz4) specification. `sequence` is `Last of byte list | Match of byte list * int * int * sequence`; `copy` appends `remaining` bytes each read `distance` back in the output so far (so distance 1 repeats the last byte); `decode` applies a sequence; `consume_match` checks input bytes against the growing output, and `consume_match_sound` proves that when it succeeds, `copy` produces the same output. `source_position` is an arithmetic helper.
It is checked by the library build, but no library module imports it: the public codec and its specification do not depend on it. Its users are the tests `lz4_model.ml` and `lz4_overlap.ml`.

notes.title: Checked match consumption
notes.text: `consume_match` accepts a match only if every input byte equals the byte `distance` back in the extended output; `consume_match_sound` proves that the output then equals what `copy` would produce from the distance alone.

what.short: A one-line alias: include Vox_lz4_spec_scan, giving the compressor model the name Vox_lz4_forward_model used by the streaming compressor.
long: The whole file is `include Vox_lz4_spec_scan`. `Vox_lz4_streaming` and `Vox_lz4_streaming_codec` refer to the [LZ4](demo:lz4) compressor model through this name, and `vox_lz4_general_roundtrip.md` describes the proof in its terms. It adds no definitions; `Vox_lz4_forward_model.from_source` is `Vox_lz4_spec_scan.from_source`.

what.short: Unverified test reference: runs the compressor model's scan with stdlib maps and records the hash candidate seen at each position.
long: A test helper for [LZ4](demo:lz4). `from_source` repeats the scan of the compressor model with `Map.Make (Int)` in place of the association list and returns an `int iarray` giving, for every visited position, the candidate the hash lookup produced (-1 elsewhere). `lz4_fast_reference.ml` feeds these hints to `Vox_lz4_general_plan.from_hints` and checks that the resulting plan equals the plans of the checked scanners.

It is compiled with the library and type-checked, but it has no contract beyond the source-length refinement on its argument, and its inner `scan` is not declared total, so it carries no proved property; its agreement with the models is tested.

what.short: A second compressor model with the same hash and match decisions as the specification's scan, building the plan from an accumulator.
long: An [LZ4](demo:lz4) compressor model used by the earlier string codec. It includes `Vox_lz4_spec_hashes`, and its `scan` makes the same decisions as `Vox_lz4_spec_scan.scan` (same `hash4`, `lookup`, `choose_match` and limits), but it is tail-recursive: completed sequences go into a `Vox_lz4_general_plan.pending` accumulator, and `build_plan` assembles the plan at the end. The result is proved valid (`valid_plan source 0`).

It is checked. `Vox_lz4_mutable_scan` and `Vox_lz4_string_scan` prove their mutable scans equal to this `scan`, and `Vox_lz4_string_codec` defines its own `compresses` relation with this model. The public `Vox_lz4` uses `Vox_lz4_spec_scan` instead; no theorem in the library equates the two `from_source` functions, and `lz4_fast_reference.ml` compares them by testing.

notes.title: Accumulating scan
notes.text: Decisions match the specification's scanner line for line; the difference is that a match is pushed onto `pending` with its anchor, and `P.build_plan` reverses the accumulator into a plan when the scan stops.

what.short: Instantiates the general LZ4 round-trip theorem at the accumulator scanner's plan and at the mutable scanner's plan.
long: Three thin wrappers over `Vox_lz4_general_roundtrip.roundtrip_plan_capacity` for [LZ4](demo:lz4): `roundtrip_capacity` and `roundtrip` use the plan from `Vox_lz4_fast_plan_model.from_source`, and `mutable_scan_roundtrip_capacity` uses `Vox_lz4_mutable_scan.from_source`. Each runs encoder and decoder and returns `None` (allocation failed) or `Some (Done, buffer)` whose first `Iarray.length source` bytes match the source.
Verified by the library build; the only caller is the test `lz4_fast_reference.ml`. It is not on the path of the public `Vox_lz4.roundtrip` theorem.

notes.title: Round trip at a capacity
notes.text: `None` is allowed by the contract, so the theorem says nothing when an allocation fails; on `Some`, decoding succeeded and reproduced the source.

what.short: Heap lemmas for LZ4 decoding: writing literals and a verified match into the output keeps the output equal to a prefix of the source.
long: Proof infrastructure for the [LZ4](demo:lz4) heap-level round trip. It re-exports `Vox_lz4_spec_match` and adds ghost lemmas about `Vox_lz4_roundtrip.output_matches`, which says the first `count` heap cells of a buffer hold the source's first `count` bytes: `output_matches_get`, `output_matches_put_outside` and `output_matches_append` for single writes, `source_matches_distance_at` for one byte of a match, and `copy_literals_preserves_source`, `copy_match_preserves_source` and `sequence_preserves_source`, which show that `Vox_lz4_spec_decode.literal_heap` and `copy_heap` extend a correct prefix to a longer correct prefix.
All lemmas are checked ghost code with `[@@decreases]` measures where recursive; they add no assumptions. `Vox_lz4_general_plan.plan_reconstructs_source` builds on them.

notes.title: A match copy reproduces the source
notes.text: The key step of the round trip: if the output holds the source up to `used` and the source repeats at `distance` for `remaining` bytes, the overlapping heap copy yields the source up to `used + remaining`. Each copied byte comes from an already-correct cell, found by `output_matches_get`.

what.short: LZ4 plan utilities: an accumulator for plans, plans from arbitrary hints, and the proof that applying a valid plan rebuilds the source.
long: Part of the [LZ4](demo:lz4) proofs. It re-exports `Vox_lz4_spec_plan` and adds `pending` (completed matches in reverse, each with its anchor), `valid_pending`, and `build_plan`, which turns a pending list and a valid suffix into a valid plan. `plan_from_hints` and `from_hints` run the specification's scan with an arbitrary `int iarray` of candidate positions in place of the hash table: any hint array yields a valid plan, because `choose_match` checks every candidate.

`apply_plan` is the ghost effect of decoding a plan on a heap (literal writes then match copies), and `plan_reconstructs_source` proves that for a valid plan, starting from an output that matches the source up to the anchor, it leaves the whole source in the buffer. Everything here is checked; `Vox_lz4_general_wire.decode_plan` uses `apply_plan` as its target.

notes.title: Plans from any hints
notes.text: The same scan as the specification's, with `S.iarray_get hints position` in place of the hash lookup. The result is proved valid whatever the hints are, which makes the round trip independent of the hash function.

notes.title: A valid plan rebuilds the source
notes.text: Induction over the plan using `sequence_preserves_source` for each match and `copy_literals_preserves_source` for the final run.

what.short: The LZ4 encoder's heap model encode_model, which writes a plan's wire bytes into a raw buffer, and an encoder with run-time capacity checks.
long: Part of the [LZ4](demo:lz4) compressor proof. It re-exports `Vox_lz4_spec_token` and defines `encode_model source anchor plan block used heap`, a ghost function returning the byte count and heap after writing the plan's tokens, extensions, literals and offsets into `block` from position `used`. The streaming compressor that `Vox_lz4.compress` runs is proved to leave exactly the state of `encode_model` for the plan of `Vox_lz4_spec_scan.from_source`.

`emit` and `encode` are an executable encoder of any valid plan into a `Vox_lz4_encode_buffer`, proved to agree with `encode_model`. They check the remaining capacity before each sequence and return `None` if it is short; `Vox_lz4_general_sized` removes those checks with the size bound. This executable encoder is used by the test `lz4_general_encode.ml`. All of it is checked; the buffer primitives it calls are trusted through `raw_memory.mli`.

notes.title: One sequence in the encoder heap model
notes.text: Mirrors `Vox_lz4_spec_wire.wire_matches_plan` write for write: token, literal extensions, literals, low and high offset bytes, match extensions. `Vox_lz4_general_bridge.model_wire` proves that bytes copied out of this heap satisfy the wire relation.

what.short: The encoded size of an LZ4 plan and bounds on it, proving that source length plus extension bytes plus 15 always suffices.
long: Proof infrastructure for the [LZ4](demo:lz4) compressor. `encoded_size source anchor plan` is the number of wire bytes of a plan. `sequence_cost_bound` and `final_cost_bound` bound one sequence's overhead, `encoded_size_loose_bound` gives size at most twice the remaining length plus 16, and `encoded_size_bound` the sharper `255 * (size - remaining) <= remaining + 255 * 16`. With `extension_count_covers` and `extension_budget`, `encoded_size_capacity` concludes that the size is at most the remaining length plus `extension_budget` plus 15, which is the capacity the encoders allocate. `encode_model_size` proves that `encode_model` advances the count by exactly `encoded_size`.

All checked ghost lemmas. Several proofs proceed by a chain of `let _ : {u : unit | ...} = ()` steps that give the SMT solver intermediate arithmetic facts. The streaming compressor and `Vox_lz4_general_sized` use these bounds to drop run-time capacity checks.

notes.title: Encoded size
notes.text: A sequence costs a token, two offset bytes, its literals and the extension bytes of both lengths; the final run costs a token, its extensions and its literals.

notes.title: The allocation size suffices
notes.text: The capacity lemma behind every encoder's single allocation of `length + extension_count length + 15` bytes. It combines the loose and sharp size bounds with `remaining < 255 * budget`.

what.short: An LZ4 plan encoder whose capacity checks are proved away: the buffer's size precondition replaces the run-time test.
long: Part of the [LZ4](demo:lz4) proofs. `emit` has the same body as `Vox_lz4_general_encode.emit` without the capacity tests: its buffer argument is refined by `encoded_size source anchor plan <= M.length b.block - b.used`, and it returns a buffer (no option) whose count and heap equal `encode_model`. `encode` allocates `length + extension_count length + 15` bytes and, using `Vox_lz4_general_cost.encoded_size_capacity`, calls `emit`; it returns `None` only if the allocation fails.
Verified by the library build. Its callers are `Vox_lz4_general_roundtrip`, `vox_lz4_checked_api.ml` and the test `lz4_fast_reference.ml`.

notes.title: Encoding with a proved capacity
notes.text: The size precondition holds from the allocation on: at each sequence `encoded_size_loose_bound` proves it for the rest of the plan, so no capacity test remains in the code.

what.short: Proof that decoding a wire laid out from any valid plan, with the heap decoder model, succeeds and leaves the source in the output buffer.
long: The heap-level decoding half of the [LZ4](demo:lz4) general round trip. It re-exports `Vox_lz4_spec_wire` and proves, about `Vox_lz4_spec_decode.decode_model`: `decode_end` (a wire matching `End` decodes to `Done` with the literals written), `decode_sequence_step` (one sequence's decoding equals a recursive call after its literals and match copy), `decode_plan` (by induction, decoding a matching wire gives `Done`, the source length and the heap `Vox_lz4_general_plan.apply_plan`), and `decode_wire_matches_source`, which combines this with `plan_reconstructs_source`. `match_token_fields` recovers the two nibbles of a `match_token`.

All checked ghost lemmas. `decode_wire_matches_source` is used by `Vox_lz4_general_roundtrip` and by `compressed_decodes` in the streaming and string codecs. The public `Vox_lz4.roundtrip` goes through the pure decoder instead (`vox_lz4_decode_bytes_roundtrip.ml`, which reuses `match_token_fields`).

notes.title: Decoding a planned wire
notes.to: P.apply_plan heap block source anchor plan} @ ghost
notes.text: The invariant carries the previous match start so the final-sequence checks of the decoder model hold: a valid plan's last match starts at most 12 bytes before the end and leaves at least five literals. The fuel only needs to be at least the remaining wire length.

notes.title: Round trip at the heap level
notes.text: From an empty buffer (`M.footprint block`), a wire satisfying `wire_matches_plan` for any valid plan decodes, at any capacity from the source length to 4,194,304, to `Done` with the source in the buffer.

what.short: Proof that bytes copied out of the encoder's heap model satisfy the LZ4 wire relation, linking the mutable compressor to compresses.
long: The bridge from the [LZ4](demo:lz4) encoder's heap model to the specification's wire relation. `model_wire` proves: if a wire array has length `(encode_model ...).count` and `Vox_lz4_heap_bytes.prefix_matches` the heap `encode_model` produced, then `Vox_lz4_spec_wire.wire_matches_plan source wire anchor used plan` holds. Its helpers are `model_preserves_earlier_byte` (the encoder model never changes cells before `used`), `model_preserves_prefix` (so a prefix match of the final heap is a prefix match of an earlier one), `end_model_wire` (the final literal run) and `encoded_size_positive`.

All checked ghost lemmas, under the hypothesis that the encoded size fits the 4,210,768-byte wire bound. `Vox_lz4_streaming_codec.compress` calls `model_wire` after copying the buffer to a string, which is the step that turns the compressor's heap contract into `Vox_lz4_spec.compresses`; `vox_lz4_checked_api.ml` and the string codec use it the same way.

notes.title: Earlier bytes are untouched
notes.text: Encoding the rest of a plan from `used` leaves every cell below `used` unchanged. This lets the proof check each sequence's bytes in the final heap after later sequences are written.

notes.title: Heap model to wire relation
notes.to: || Vox_lz4_spec_wire.wire_matches_plan source wire anchor used plan} @ ghost
notes.text: The statement used by the public compressor: a string whose bytes are the encoder model's heap prefix, of exactly the model's length, satisfies the wire layout of the plan. It is proved by induction over the plan, with `end_model_wire` for the last run.

what.short: An executable LZ4 round-trip theorem for any valid plan: encode it, decode the wire, and the decoded buffer holds the source.
long: The general round trip of the [LZ4](demo:lz4) proofs. `roundtrip_plan_capacity source plan capacity` encodes a valid plan with `Vox_lz4_general_sized.encode`, snapshots the encoded buffer into an array, decodes it with `Vox_lz4_packed.decode` at a capacity from the source length to 4,194,304, releases the encoded buffer and returns the decoded one. Its contract: `None` (an allocation failed) or `Some (status, decoded)` with `status === Done`, the decoded length equal to the source length and `Vox_lz4_roundtrip.output_matches` for the whole source. `roundtrip_plan` fixes the capacity to the source length, and `roundtrip_hints` applies it to `Vox_lz4_general_plan.from_hints`, so it holds for any hint array.

Verified by the library build; the proof is the ghost block combining `encoded_size_capacity`, `encode_model_size`, `Vox_lz4_general_bridge.model_wire` and `Vox_lz4_general_wire.decode_wire_matches_source`. Because the theorem quantifies over all valid plans, it covers every scanner that produces one. It is used by `Vox_lz4_fast_plan_roundtrip` and the test `lz4_general_roundtrip.ml`; the public `Vox_lz4.roundtrip` is a separate ghost theorem over the pure decoder model.

notes.title: The theorem
notes.text: The contract quantifies over every plan satisfying `valid_plan source 0`. The `None` case covers allocation failure in either the encoder or the decoder.

notes.title: The proof
notes.text: Four lemmas: the capacity suffices, the encoder model's count is the encoded size, the snapshot satisfies the wire layout, and the heap decoder model reconstructs the source from that wire.

what.short: Implementation of the public Vox_lz4 interface: binds compress to the streaming compressor and decompression to the string decoder, and composes them.
long: The implementation behind [the public interface](src:verification/library/vox_lz4.mli) of [the LZ4 demo](demo:lz4). `compress` is `Vox_lz4_streaming_codec.compress_string`; `decompress_verified` is `Vox_lz4_string_decode.decode_string`; `decompress` checks its optional capacity against `max_block_size` (4,194,304), returns `Error Invalid_capacity` outside 0 to 4,194,304, and otherwise calls `decompress_verified`, with the default capacity 4,194,304. `roundtrip` re-exports the total ghost theorem `Vox_lz4_streaming_roundtrip.roundtrip`, which is `Vox_lz4_decode_bytes_roundtrip.roundtrip`. The types `malformed` and `decode_error` are re-exported from the decoder.

Verified: each function is checked here against its public refinement type. `compress_decompress` runs both halves, calls `roundtrip` inside `ghost_`, and discharges the `Error` branch with `unreachable_ ()`, so the checker proves that decoding a fresh compression at capacity `V.length source` succeeds and returns the source's contents. The file declares nothing trusted; the trusted items beneath it are the `Raw_memory` externals used by the two buffers and `Vox_lz4_string_copy.copy_prefix`. The codec functions are specified for normal return only: they can raise `Out_of_memory`, and `compress` and `compress_decompress` raise `Invalid_argument` above 4 MiB.

notes.title: decompress: optional capacity
notes.text: The refinement matches on the optional argument `c` as passed. The range check here is what lets the contract promise `Error Invalid_capacity` exactly outside 0 to 4,194,304, and `matches_model` at the given or default capacity otherwise.

notes.title: compress_decompress: the round trip, executed
notes.text: The ghost call to `R.roundtrip` supplies both facts the checker needs: `decoded` is `Ok`, which makes the `Error` branch provably unreachable, and its contents equal the source's, which is the return refinement. The size check is needed because `decompress_verified` requires a capacity of at most 4,194,304.

what.short: The public compressor: runs the streaming encoder into raw memory, copies the used prefix into a string, and proves those bytes are the compressor model's wire.
long: Provides `compress_string`, which `Vox_lz4.compress` calls, with the contract `Vox_lz4_spec.compresses source wire`, and the ghost-indexed `compress`, whose result satisfies `Vox_lz4_spec_wire.wire_matches_plan model wire 0 0 (Vox_lz4_spec_scan.from_source model)`. `compress` calls `Vox_lz4_streaming.encode`, which fills a `Vox_lz4_encode_buffer` in raw memory, copies the `used` prefix into a fresh string with the trusted `Vox_lz4_string_copy.copy_prefix`, and then, in ghost code, uses `Vox_lz4_general_cost` and `Vox_lz4_general_bridge.model_wire` to turn the heap-level statement about the buffer into the byte-level `wire_matches_plan` statement about the string. The module includes `Vox_lz4_spec`, so it also re-exports the specification relations.

Verified; on the public path of [the LZ4 demo](demo:lz4). The trusted items it relies on are `copy_prefix` and the `Raw_memory` externals under the buffer. Allocation failure in `encode` (`None`) becomes `Out_of_memory`; an exception from the copy releases the buffer and re-raises it. `compressed_decodes`, a ghost lemma relating `compresses` to the heap decoder model `Vox_lz4_spec_decode.decode_model`, has no caller in the library or the tests at HEAD.

notes.title: Encode, copy once, release
notes.text: The plan is ghost: `Vox_lz4_spec_scan.from_source` is never run. After the single copy into a GC string, the three ghost calls transfer the encoder's heap postcondition to the string's contents; `copy_prefix`'s `prefix_matches` result is the link. The comment explains why the exception handler returns `Error exn` and leaves the release to the code after it.

what.short: The compressor's scan loop over a string and a mutable 65,536-slot hash table, writing LZ4 sequences into raw memory as it goes, proved equal to the model's encoding.
long: `encode` allocates a `Vox_lz4_encode_buffer` of `length + extension_count length + 15` bytes and an owned `int` table (`Borrow_iarray.Owned_array`) initialized from `Vox_lz4_mutable_scan.empty_table`, then runs `scan`. `scan` follows `Vox_lz4_spec_scan.scan` step by step: it hashes four bytes with `Vox_lz4_string_match.hash4`, reads and overwrites that table slot, tries the previous position with `Vox_lz4_string_match.choose_match`, and on a match calls `emit_head`, which writes the token, literal-length extensions, literals, the little-endian offset (`split_distance`, by integer division) and match-length extensions. At the end it writes the last literal run with `Vox_lz4_string_encode.emit`. The table is related to the model's list of `(hash, position)` entries by `Vox_lz4_mutable_scan.agrees`.

The contract of `scan` equates the final count and ghost heap with `Vox_lz4_general_encode.encode_model` of the plan that `Vox_lz4_spec_scan.scan` returns. That plan, the `entries` list and the `fuel` measure are all ghost, so no plan is built at run time. `emit_head_capacity` is the arithmetic lemma that the remaining capacity covers one sequence header. Verified; on the public path of [the LZ4 demo](demo:lz4), called only by `Vox_lz4_streaming_codec`.

notes.title: Offset bytes by division
notes.text: The runtime computes the two offset bytes with `/` and `-`; the refinement proves the record equal to the specification's `Vox_lz4_spec_token.split_distance`, which is only evaluated in ghost code.

notes.title: scan: contract against the scanner model
notes.text: The precondition ties the owned table to the ghost `entries` (`T.agrees`) and requires capacity for the rest of the model's plan; the postcondition says the buffer ends exactly as `encode_model` of `Vox_lz4_spec_scan.scan` from this state. This is where the implementation is bound to the compressor model's positions, hashes and match choices.

what.short: The public decoder: parses an LZ4 block from a string into a raw buffer, proved to agree with the decoder model in status, length and every output byte.
long: `decode_string wire capacity`, which `Vox_lz4.decompress_verified` calls, returns `Ok` of a string or `Error` of a `decode_error`, with the contract `Vox_lz4_spec.matches_model wire capacity r`. Below it, `decode` allocates a `Vox_lz4_buffer` of `capacity` bytes and `decode_sequences` walks the block: the token, `read_length` and `read_extended_length` for extended lengths, `copy_literals` from the input string, the two offset bytes, and `copy_match` for back-references, possibly overlapping, read byte by byte from the buffer. Each piece is specified against the heap model `Vox_lz4_spec_decode` (`literal_heap`, `copy_heap`, `decode_model`): the returned status kind, `used` count and ghost heap equal the model's.

`decode_string` then connects the heap model to the specification's pure byte model: ghost calls to `Vox_lz4_decode_bytes_proof.decode` and `observations` show that the heap model and `Vox_lz4_spec_decode_bytes.decode_model` agree, and that the string produced by the trusted `Vox_lz4_string_copy.copy_prefix` matches the pure model's bytes. The `fuel` of `decode_sequences` and `read_extended_length` is ghost; `Vox_lz4_decode_bytes_proof.read_length_cursor` justifies its decrease. Verified; on the public path of [the LZ4 demo](demo:lz4). The reason and position inside `Malformed` are computed here and left unconstrained by the contract. The module aliases `EB` and `Snapshot` are unused.

notes.title: decode_sequences: agreement with the heap model
notes.from: let rec decode_sequences : (model : char iarray) @ ghost ->
notes.text: The input is read through `Vox_string_view.get` while the ghost `model` is its contents. The postcondition maps each error to the model's status kind (never `Invalid_capacity`) and equates buffer identity, count and ghost heap with `Vox_lz4_spec_decode.decode_model`.

what.short: Trusted interface: copy_prefix copies the first count initialized bytes of a raw buffer into a fresh GC string, implemented by allocation and memcpy in runtime/pref.c.
long: Declares one `external`, `copy_prefix block count permission`, and its contract is trusted. Given a read-only ghost borrow of a permission whose heap covers the whole block and whose first `count` bytes are initialized (`Vox_lz4_spec_storage.initialized`), it returns a string of length `count` whose characters match those heap bytes (`Vox_lz4_heap_bytes.prefix_matches`). The permission stays with the caller and the buffer stays allocated. The contract describes normal return; the C code can raise `Out_of_memory`, and both callers catch it.

The implementation is `caml_raw_memory_copy_string` in `runtime/pref.c`: it roots the handle, allocates the string with `caml_alloc_string`, and then `memcpy`s from the raw pointer, which it reads after the allocation. The bytecode stub takes the extra erased token argument. This is the one copy of the output in [the LZ4 demo](demo:lz4): `Vox_lz4_streaming_codec.compress` and `Vox_lz4_string_decode.decode_string` both end with it. It is part of the demo's trusted base, and the meaning of its contract rests on the definitions in `vox_lz4_spec_storage.ml` and [vox_lz4_heap_bytes.ml](src:verification/library/vox_lz4_heap_bytes.ml).

what.short: Defines prefix_matches: the first count characters of a char iarray equal, byte for byte, the initialized cells of a raw buffer in a ghost heap.
long: One ghost definition, `prefix_matches values heap block count`, recursive on `count`: for each index `i` below `count`, `values` has a character `c` at `i`, the heap cell at `Raw_memory.location block i` holds `Some byte`, and `Vox_lz4_spec_parse.byte_of_char c = byte`. `[@def]` generates `prefix_matches_def` for proofs. It is the vocabulary of the postcondition of the trusted `Vox_lz4_string_copy.copy_prefix`, so a reviewer of the trusted base of [the LZ4 demo](demo:lz4) reads this definition to know what that external promises; the review boundary document lists it for that reason.

Verified (total, with a termination measure); it contains no assumption. Lemmas about it (`prefix_matches_get`, `prefix_matches_prefix`, `prefix_set_next`, `prefix_matches_put_outside`) are in `Vox_lz4_snapshot` and `Vox_lz4_roundtrip`.

what.short: Decoder output buffer: a raw-memory block of at most 4 MiB with a ghost permission, a used count, and the invariant that the first used bytes are initialized.
long: Type `t` is a record `{block; permission; used}` refined so that `used <= Raw_memory.length block <= 4194304`, the permission's heap covers every byte of the block and the marker location `location block (-1)`, and the first `used` bytes are initialized (`Vox_lz4_spec_storage.initialized`). The lemmas `initialized_get`, `write_preserves_initialized` and `append_initialized` maintain the invariant.

Verified; the trusted parts are the `Raw_memory` externals it calls and the assumed `location_law`. Used by the public decoder `Vox_lz4_string_decode` and by the iarray decoder `Vox_lz4_packed`. Verified; the `roundtrip` binding is on the public path of [the LZ4 demo](demo:lz4).

what.short: The round-trip proof: decoding a wire laid out from a valid plan yields the source bytes, stated over strings and the pure byte-list decoder model with no raw memory.
long: The main theorem of [the LZ4 demo](demo:lz4). It works over the allocation-independent models only: `Vox_lz4_spec_decode_bytes.decode_model`, which returns a status, a count and a reversed byte list, and `Vox_lz4_spec_wire.wire_matches_plan`. `decode_plan` is the induction over the plan: if the wire matches the plan at a cursor and the byte list matches the source up to `anchor` (`matches_bytes`), decoding reaches `Done` with count equal to the source length and bytes matching the source. Its steps are `decode_end` (the final literal run), `decode_sequence_step` (token, lengths and offset of one sequence), `literals`, and `matches`, which uses `source_matches_distance` to show that a back-reference copy, overlapping or not, reproduces the source. The side condition on `last_match_start` carries the end-of-block rules (the last match starts at least 12 bytes before the end and is followed by at least five literals).

`decode_wire` starts the induction at cursor 0; `equal_bytes` turns two byte-list matches into equality of `char iarray`s with `Vox_iarray.extensional`; `wire_roundtrip` combines these with `Vox_lz4_spec.matches_model_def` for any plan; `roundtrip` instantiates the plan with `Vox_lz4_spec_scan.from_source` under `Vox_lz4_spec.compresses`. All are total ghost functions, verified, with no heap or allocation. `Vox_lz4_streaming_roundtrip.roundtrip` re-exports `roundtrip` as `Vox_lz4.roundtrip`. Token and length-reading lemmas (`read_literal_length`, `literal_token_fields`, `wire_byte_get`) come from `Vox_lz4_roundtrip`.

notes.title: decode_plan: the induction
notes.text: The invariant pairs a position in the plan with a position in the wire and a decoded prefix of the source. The theorem is stated for every plan satisfying `wire_matches_plan`, so it does not depend on how the compressor chose its matches.

notes.title: roundtrip: the public theorem
notes.text: This is the statement exported as `Vox_lz4.roundtrip`. Unfolding `compresses` gives `wire_matches_plan` for the plan `Vox_lz4_spec_scan.from_source`, and `wire_roundtrip` does the rest.

what.short: Proves that the heap decoder model (bytes in a raw buffer) and the pure byte-list decoder model agree on status, count and every output byte.
long: `heap_matches heap block used reversed` says the heap's first `used` cells of `block` hold the bytes of `reversed`, last byte first. The lemmas `put_outside`, `append`, `read_distance`, `literals` and `matches` show that `Vox_lz4_spec_decode.literal_heap` and `copy_heap` preserve it in step with `Vox_lz4_spec_decode_bytes.literal_bytes` and `copy_bytes`. `decode` is the induction over the decoder: from matching states, `Vox_lz4_spec_decode_bytes.decode_model` and `Vox_lz4_spec_decode.decode_model` return the same kind and count, and the final heap matches the pure byte list. `observations` shows that for any `char iarray`, the pure `matches_bytes` and the heap `Vox_lz4_heap_bytes.prefix_matches` are the same boolean.

This bridge lets the public decoder, which is proved against the heap model, meet the specification, which mentions only the pure model: `Vox_lz4_string_decode.decode_string` calls `decode` and `observations` in ghost code. `initial_observations` packages the two at the initial state; the review boundary document names it, but no module calls it. `read_length_cursor` and `extended_cursor` prove that a successful length read moves the cursor forward within the input, which justifies the ghost fuel in `Vox_lz4_string_decode`, and `remaining_length` names the extended-length read used there. All are total ghost functions, verified. Part of [the LZ4 demo](demo:lz4).

what.short: Heap and wire lemmas shared by the LZ4 proofs, plus an early round-trip proof for the literal-only or initial-run encoder of Vox_lz4_packed_encode.
long: Most of the file is a lemma library over ghost heaps and wire bytes: `extra_count` (the number of length-extension bytes), `heap_put_at` and `heap_put_other` (from `Raw_memory.location_law`), the `literal_heap_*` and `extension_heap_*` frame, substitution and wire-layout lemmas for the encoders' heap models, `snapshot_at`, the token and length-reading lemmas `literal_token_fields`, `match_token_fields`, `read_literal_length`, `read_match_length` and `wire_byte_get`, and the definition `output_matches`. The public proofs use these: `Vox_lz4_general_bridge`, `Vox_lz4_general_wire` and `Vox_lz4_decode_bytes_roundtrip` call them, and `Vox_lz4_streaming_codec.compressed_decodes` is stated with `output_matches`.

The rest is an executable round trip for a small encoder: `literal_layout`, `literal_wire`, `run_layout`, `run_wire`, `decode_literal_wire`, `decode_run_wire` and `roundtrip`, which encodes a `char iarray` with `Vox_lz4_packed_encode.encode` (a literal-only block, or one initial run of a repeated byte at offset 1), snapshots the wire with `Vox_lz4_snapshot.snapshot_prefix`, decodes it with `Vox_lz4_packed.decode`, and proves that the decoded heap holds the source. That `roundtrip` function is off the public path; the test `lz4_snapshot.ml` runs it, and its `snapshot_prefix` call is how this file reaches the trusted `Vox_lz4_snapshot.char_of_byte`. Verified. notes.text: Encodes, snapshots, and decodes with the iarray decoder, all at run time; the ghost block after decoding picks the layout lemma for the plan `plan_of_source` chose. None of this is on the path of `Vox_lz4`.

what.short: Copies an encode buffer's used prefix into a char iarray through an owned slice, with prefix_matches lemmas; declares a trusted char_of_byte external.
long: `snapshot_prefix buffer` allocates a `char iarray` of `used` characters, fills it with `fill` inside `Borrow_iarray.Owned_array.with_mut` (reading each byte with `Raw_memory.read` and converting it with `char_of_byte`), and returns it with the unchanged buffer, proving `Vox_lz4_heap_bytes.prefix_matches values heap block used`. It is an in-OCaml counterpart of the trusted `Vox_lz4_string_copy.copy_prefix` that produces an iarray. The lemmas `prefix_matches_get`, `prefix_matches_prefix`, `prefix_set_outside` and `prefix_set_next` reason about `prefix_matches`.

Trusted: `external char_of_byte` (`%identity`) with the contract `byte_of_char c = value`. It states the inverse direction of the pair in `vox_lz4_spec_parse.ml`, which gives only `char_of_byte (byte_of_char c) = c`, so it is an additional assumption. The public codec never calls it: `snapshot_prefix` is used by `Vox_lz4_roundtrip.roundtrip`, `Vox_lz4_checked_api` and `Vox_lz4_general_roundtrip`, all off the public path. The public compressor proof does use this file's verified lemmas `prefix_matches_prefix` (through `Vox_lz4_general_bridge`) and `prefix_matches_get` (through `Vox_lz4_roundtrip.snapshot_at`). Part of [the LZ4 demo](demo:lz4).

notes.title: Trusted byte-to-char conversion
notes.text: An identity primitive whose contract is assumed. It is true for bytes 0 to 255, which `M.byte` guarantees, but no proof connects it to the `char_of_byte` and `byte_of_char` declared in `Vox_lz4_spec_parse`.

what.short: An LZ4 decoder over a char iarray input into a Vox_lz4_buffer, proved equal to the heap decoder model; it also re-exports that model's types.
long: `Vox_lz4_packed` includes `Vox_lz4_spec_decode`, so it re-exports the heap decoder model (`decode_model`, `literal_heap`, `copy_heap`, the `status` constructors `Done`, `Malformed` and `Output_limit`, and `length_result`). Its own code is a decoder for input already held as a `char iarray`: `copy_literals`, `copy_match` (an overlapping copy through `Vox_lz4_buffer.observe` and `append`), `decode_sequences` and `decode`, each with a contract equating its status, count and ghost heap with the model's. It returns a bare `status`, without the error reason and position the public decoder reports.

Verified. The public decoder `Vox_lz4_string_decode` opens this module for the model's types and constructors and does its own parsing over a string; `Vox_lz4_packed.decode` itself is off the public path. It is called by `Vox_lz4_roundtrip.roundtrip`, `Vox_lz4_checked_api.decode` and the tests `lz4_packed.ml` and `lz4_fast_decoder_reference.ml`. Part of [the LZ4 demo](demo:lz4).
