notes.text: The same statement as the public decoder's, with a run-time `fuel` and a `char iarray` input. `Vox_lz4_string_decode.decode_sequences` is the string-input version of this function.

what.short: A first verified LZ4 encoder (literal-only, or one initial run at offset 1) and the literal and extension emitters and heap models that later encoders reuse.
long: Defines the ghost heap models `literal_heap` and `extension_heap` (what writing a literal range or a length extension does to the buffer's heap), `same_prefix` with its lemmas, the emitters `copy_literals` and `emit_extensions` (255-bytes then the remainder, proved equal to `extension_heap`), and `match_token`. On these it builds a small encoder: `plan_of_source` returns `Initial_run run_end` when the source has at least 13 bytes and starts with a run of equal bytes ending at `run_end` with 5 <= `run_end` <= length - 5, and `Literal_only` otherwise; `encode` writes that plan into a `Vox_lz4_encode_buffer`, proved equal to `encode_model`. It includes `Vox_lz4_spec_bytes`.

Verified. The small encoder (`plan_of_source`, `encode_literals`, `encode`) is off the public path; `Vox_lz4_roundtrip.roundtrip` uses it. The public compressor does use `emit_extensions` (from `Vox_lz4_streaming` and `Vox_lz4_string_encode`) and, through `Vox_lz4_general_encode`, `copy_literals`, `literal_heap` and `extension_heap`. Part of [the LZ4 demo](demo:lz4).

notes.title: emit_extensions
notes.text: Writes an LZ4 length extension: 255 while at least 255 remains, then the remainder. The public compressor calls this function for both literal and match lengths.

what.short: An alternative compress/decode pair with unrefined types, built on the hint-based plan encoder and the iarray decoder; no module or test refers to it.
long: `compress` copies the string into a `char iarray`, computes match hints with an ordinary mutable `Array` hash table, builds a plan with `Vox_lz4_general_plan.from_hints`, encodes it with `Vox_lz4_general_sized.encode`, snapshots the buffer with `Vox_lz4_snapshot.snapshot_prefix` and copies the result into a string with `String.init`; a ghost block checks `wire_matches_plan` for that plan locally. `decode` runs `Vox_lz4_packed.decode` and copies the output with `Bytes.set` and `Char.chr`. Neither function has a refined result type, so the module exports no guarantee.

The file is checked with the rest of the library, but nothing in `verification/library` or the test suite refers to `Vox_lz4_checked_api`; it is off the public path of [the LZ4 demo](demo:lz4). Through `snapshot_prefix` it reaches the trusted `Vox_lz4_snapshot.char_of_byte`.

what.short: Review guide to the LZ4 demo: specification modules, separate proof support, and the trusted primitives and runtime mechanisms.
long: Documentation for [the LZ4 demo](demo:lz4). It lists the ten semantic modules (`vox_lz4_spec.ml` through `vox_lz4_spec_scan.ml`) in reading order; locates the checked extension lemma in the separate `vox_lz4_match_proof.ml` module; names the transitive semantic primitives (`vox_string_view.mli`, `vox_sequence.mli`, `vox_iarray.mli`, byte conversion in `vox_lz4_spec_parse.ml`, the hash word primitives) and the executable ownership contracts to review (`pref.mli`, `ghost_pref.mli`, `raw_memory.mli`, `borrow_iarray.mli`, `vox_lz4_string_copy.mli`) with their C and backend implementations. It also states the 4 MiB domain, the normal-return scope of the specification, the GC finalizer that reclaims raw buffers after exceptions, and the tests (`lz4_boundary.ml`, `lz4_finalizers.ml`) that check a public-only client.

Two details differ from the code at HEAD. It calls `Vox_lz4_decode_bytes_proof.initial_observations` the checked equivalence theorem; the decoder invokes the lemmas `decode` and `observations` directly, and `initial_observations` has no caller. It omits the `char_of_byte` external in `vox_lz4_snapshot.ml`, which the public codec never calls and which the catalogue page does list.

what.short: Overview of the verified mutable LZ4 codec: public contracts, proof structure, runtime boundary, tests, and a throughput benchmark against the original codec.
long: The overview document of [the LZ4 demo](demo:lz4), titled "Verified mutable LZ4"; its subject is the whole public codec. It states the public specification (`compress`, `decompress_verified`, `decompress`, `roundtrip`, `compress_decompress`), outlines the proof (the streaming scan in `Vox_lz4_streaming`, the string decoder `Vox_lz4_string_decode`, the heap-to-bytes bridge `Vox_lz4_decode_bytes_proof`, the pure round trip `Vox_lz4_decode_bytes_roundtrip`), describes the runtime boundary (raw memory, the one final copy by `caml_raw_memory_copy_string`, the finalizer), and lists the differential tests and a native benchmark from 2026-09-25 against `vox_lz4_baseline.ml`.

It names `Vox_lz4_forward_model` as the scanner model; that module is `include Vox_lz4_spec_scan`, and the code states its contracts with `Vox_lz4_spec_scan` directly. The benchmark figures are recorded measurements that the build does not recheck.

what.short: Core union-find functor: union by rank with full path compression under a fixed ghost capacity, with a credit bank that holds exactly four times the potential.
long: `Vox_union_find.Make (C)` is the core of [online union-find](demo:online-union-find) and implements [vox_union_find.mli](src:verification/library/vox_union_find.mli). The state `t` is an unboxed record of the worker's `W.resource` (the ghost heap token and the credit `bank`) and ghost fields: `paths` (one parent path per element, the proof's model of the forest), `capacity` N, `alpha`, `spent` and `events`. It exports `create`, `reparameterize`, `make_set`, `find` and `union`; `link` is internal. Each operation merges the caller's fee into the bank, calls the run-time code in `Vox_union_find_worker`, splits off exactly four times the new `Vox_union_find_bank.potential` as the new bank, and returns the rest as `refund`. Every contract states `account r + refund = account + fee`, where `account` is `spent` plus the bank, and `account_bounds` gives `ticks <= account`.

`valid` is the invariant that carries the analysis. `prepare_find` packages the amortization step of a find: the charge `4d + 2` is at most four times `Vox_union_find_amortized.release` plus `find_fee alpha`, and compression lowers the potential by exactly that release. `union` ticks one credit itself and then calls `find` twice and `link`; `create` ticks one. The fees are `create` 1, `make_set` 3, `find` `4a + 8`, `link` `4a + 7` and `union` `12a + 24`, with a = `alpha`. Each contract also states the event it appends to `events`.

Verified. Nothing here is `external` or assumed; the file inherits the trust of the worker (the `Ghost_pref` cell primitives, `Pref.equal`, and the placement of charges, which is a cost model). `reparameterize` moves the structure to a ghost capacity at most twice as large and is called only by the online layer when it doubles its epoch. The operations are not total, so their contracts hold on normal return.

what.short: The run-time union-find code: find with full path compression, link by rank, and allocation, each paying hand-placed credit charges from a ghost bank.
long: `Vox_union_find_worker.Make (C)` holds the only code of [online union-find](demo:online-union-find) that does work at run time. Its `resource` has two ghost fields: the `Ghost_pref` token `memory` that owns the nodes, and the credit token `bank`. A node is `Root rank` or `Link (rank, parent)`. `find` follows parent links recursively and rewrites each nonroot node it visits to point at the root; it takes a ghost `Vox_union_find_model.path` as the witness of the parent chain and terminates by `[@@decreases depth]`. `link` points the root of smaller rank at the other and increments the rank on a tie. `allocate` creates a `Root 0` node.

The charges are the cost model. `find` calls `C.tick` twice on entering each node and twice more for each pointer it rewrites, so a find that follows d links costs `cost d = 4d + 2`. `allocate` ticks three times. `link` removes 7 credits in one `charge` (a `C.split` whose split-off part is dropped) before it tests `Pref.equal x y`, so linking a root to itself also costs 7. The contracts state these amounts exactly, together with the resulting heap (`M.compressed`, `M.linked`, `H.put`).

Verified against trusted contracts: the `Ghost_pref` cell operations `empty`, `read`, `write` and `alloc` (C primitives), `Pref.equal` (physical equality, `%eq`), and the abstract credit interface `Vox_big_credits.S`, whose implementation `Vox_big_credits.Make` is itself verified code with no externals. Which steps call `C.tick`, and how many times, is a modelling choice; no check relates it to the instructions the compiled code executes. The match fallback in `link` is `unreachable_ ()`, which the checker proves dead. The functions are not total, so their contracts hold on normal return.

This is the inverse-Ackermann potential of Tarjan's analysis (as in CLRS §21.4), on the clamped hierarchy of `Vox_ackermann`. In [online union-find](demo:online-union-find) the core's bank holds exactly four credits per unit of it (`Vox_union_find.valid`).

what.short: Per-node inverse-Ackermann potential: level, index and phi of a nonroot from its rank and its parent's rank, and how they change as the parent's rank grows or the capacity grows.
long: For a nonroot of rank r ≥ 1 whose parent has rank p, `node_level` is the largest k < alpha with `A_k(r) <= p`, and `node_index` the largest t in [1, r] with `A_level` iterated t times on r at most p, where A is `Vox_ackermann.iter cap`, clamped at the capacity. `node_phi` is `(alpha − level) · r − index`, and 0 at rank 0. `analyze` proves the ranges: 0 ≤ level < alpha, 1 ≤ index ≤ r and 0 ≤ phi ≤ alpha · r.

`compression` is the main per-node fact: when the parent's rank grows, the level does not fall and phi does not rise, and phi drops by at least one once the parent's rank reaches the next iterate. `repeated_level` specializes it: a node whose level recurs higher up its path loses at least one unit when it is pointed at the root. `level_cap`, `index_cap` and `reparameterize` show that level and index do not depend on the cap while ranks are below it, so a larger cap with `alpha` raised from a to b ≤ a + 1 adds exactly `(b − a) · rank` to phi. Verified ghost arithmetic over `Bigint`; used by `Vox_union_find_bank` and `Vox_union_find_path_cost` in [online union-find](demo:online-union-find).

what.short: Bounds the length of a compressed path by the potential it releases plus alpha, by counting the distinct Ackermann levels of its edges.
long: A path is abstracted as a list of `edge`s, each the rank of a node of positive rank and the rank of its parent; `chain` says the ranks increase up to the root's. `loss` is the total drop of `Vox_union_find_potential.node_phi` when every node is re-pointed at the root, and `levels` is the sorted set of the edges' levels (built with `Vox_union_find_levels`). `release` shows that an edge whose level occurs again higher up loses at least one unit. `counting` concludes that the number of edges is at most `loss` plus the number of distinct levels, and `bound` that it is at most `loss + alpha`, because the levels lie in [0, alpha).

This is the counting step of the inverse-Ackermann analysis: along a path, only the highest node of each level can fail to pay for itself. Verified ghost arithmetic; used by `Vox_union_find_amortized.find_bound` in [online union-find](demo:online-union-find).

what.short: Ghost model of the union-find heap: nodes, parent paths as witnesses, depth, full path compression and linking as heap updates, with their basic lemmas.
long: `node` is `Root of int | Link of int * node P.t`: a rank, and for a link the parent. An element `elem` is a `Ghost_pref` pointer to a node. what.short: Online union-find under a growing ghost capacity, with saved credits for the potential increase and a private projection to the pure partition.
long: `Vox_union_find_online.Make (C)` implements [vox_union_find_online.mli](src:verification/library/vox_union_find_online.mli) and is the layer beneath `Vox_connectivity` in [online union-find](demo:online-union-find). Its state is the core `Vox_union_find.t`, a ghost credit token `savings` and a ghost `epoch` E. `valid` requires the core's capacity to be `min(E, max_int)`, E < 2 · size once the structure is nonempty, and `savings >= 8 · size − 4 · (E − 1)`. Payments are exact: `create` 1, `make_set` 11, `find` `find_fee s` and `union` `union_fee s`. Every refund from the core goes to savings, so `account` (the core's account plus savings) grows by exactly the fee.

`make_set` puts 8 of its 11 credits in savings and pays 3 to the core's `make_set`. When the structure is full (size equal to the capacity) it doubles E, takes `4 · E` (old epoch) from savings, which the invariant guarantees, and pays them to `Vox_union_find.reparameterize`, which needs at most four credits per element; the remainder returns to savings. No run-time node moves. `fee_bounds` shows `find_fee s <= 4a + 12` and `union_fee s <= 12a + 36` where a is the inverse Ackermann of any population bound at least the current size: the capacity can be up to twice that bound, and doubling raises `alpha` by at most one.

The file also defines private forest snapshots and transitions, and `partition` projects their paths to private `Vox_partition.bindings`. `partition_valid`, `partition_size`, `partition_contains` and `partition_root` relate that projection to the online observations. `partition_added`, `partition_found` and `partition_joined` prove singleton insertion, exact model preservation by find, and class merging. `Vox_connectivity` exposes class-list snapshots and relational contracts and retains abstract forest cost observations under `Cost`. `create` checks `max_int >= 1` at run time and raises `Invalid_argument` otherwise, because `max_int` carries no refinement.

It accompanies [online union-find](demo:online-union-find) as supporting material for the fixed-capacity layers and is off the path of the public interface: no library module uses it, and the tests `union_find.ml` and `union_find_online.ml` apply it to the core and to `Vox_union_find_simple`.

It is a separate, simpler structure beside [online union-find](demo:online-union-find): no library module uses it, and only the tests `union_find_online.ml` and `union_find_online_rejected.ml` do, as the fixed-capacity comparison for the online layer. Each operation passes the exact fee to the core and merges the core's refund into `savings`, so `account` (the core's account plus savings) grows by exactly the fee; `valid` is the core's. `fee_bounds` uses `Vox_ackermann.inverse_order` to show that the fees equal `A.find_fee a` and `A.union_fee a` for any a meeting the inverse's specification. what.short: Reader's guide to the HTTP demo: review order, the supported request subset, streaming, budget and error conventions, the public laws, and the trust boundary.
long: Documentation for [the HTTP parser](demo:http). The review order begins with the grammar in `vox_http_spec.ml`, the pure machine in `vox_http_model.ml` and the contracts in `vox_http.mli`. It describes Content-Length framing, rejection of every Transfer-Encoding, the 16,384-byte message budget, the 8,192-byte body limit and error precedence.

The public transition specifies CRLF failures and message-budget exhaustion exactly. The guide also explains the private simulation connecting the executable Driver to that model, the derived public laws and the trust boundary.

what.short: The HTTP/1.1 request grammar as executable definitions: byte classes, request and header lines, Content-Length framing, serialization and well_formed.
long: Defines the request record (`request_line`, `headers` as a list of byte lists, `body`), the outcome types `malformed`, `resource`, `framing` and `status`, and the grammar: `valid_request_line`, `header` and `valid_header`, `decimal` and `content_length`, `frame_fields` and `framing`, `serialize` with `wire_headers` and `header_prefix`, and the well-formedness predicates `safe_line`, `header_lines`, `sized`, `fits` and `well_formed`. `content_lengths_match` is a ghost predicate used by the `body_agreement` law. Protocol strings are byte lists: `[72; 84; 84; 80; 47; 49; 46; 49]` is `HTTP/1.1`.

This is the specification side of [the HTTP parser](demo:http). Every definition is a `let[@def]`, so the checker generates its defining equation, and the file is checked against [vox_http_spec.mli](src:verification/library/vox_http_spec.mli), which states those equations. It is verified and contains no externals or assumptions. The executable parser calls `valid_request_line`, `valid_header` and `framing` from this module at run time, so these definitions are also the line grammar the parser runs; the proofs in `vox_http.ml` cover the byte machine around them.

notes.title: Framing and its error precedence
notes.text: `framing` first rejects any Transfer-Encoding (with a separate error when Content-Length is also present), then `frame_fields` walks the header lines in order: it requires exactly one nonempty Host, parses each Content-Length with `content_length`, and rejects disagreeing repeats. The result is `Length n`, `Bad e` or `Too_large r`; the parser reports exactly this outcome when it reaches the empty line.

notes.title: well_formed
notes.text: The predicate the soundness and completeness laws are stated with: a valid request line and header lines with no CR, LF or out-of-range byte, framing that yields `Length n`, a body of exactly `n` bytes, and a serialization of at most 16,384 bytes. `sized` and `fits` count by recursion on the list, so the budget is stated without `Bigint`.

what.short: The HTTP request grammar stated as one checked equation per definition (token_def, framing_def, well_formed_def and so on).
long: For each definition in [vox_http_spec.ml](src:verification/library/vox_http_spec.ml) this interface declares the function `@@ total` and a lemma `<name>_def` whose refinement is its defining equation. The compiler checks the implementation against it, so the equations are verified facts. `content_lengths_match` is declared with a `bool @ ghost` result, so only proof code can use it.
The [HTTP catalogue page](demo:http) shows the shorter definitions from `vox_http_spec.ml`. These checked equations expose the same meanings to clients that see only the interfaces.

notes.title: The equation for well_formed
notes.text: The predicate that the public soundness law guarantees for every `Complete request` and that the completeness law `roundtrip` assumes. Every name it mentions has its own `_def` equation earlier in this file.

what.short: Implementation and proofs of the incremental HTTP parser: the executable Driver simulates the public pure model.
long: The public pure machine is defined in [vox_http_model.ml](src:verification/library/vox_http_model.ml). `Internal` proves its accounting, request soundness, round-trip and chunking laws. Reachability and storage invariants stay inside this implementation.

`Driver` runs the parser with reversed accumulators. Its simulation proof connects each result to the forward-order pure machine. Public `feed` executes the driver and guarantees the pure machine’s next state and remaining input. Proof calls on the execution path are erased.
The [HTTP interface](src:verification/library/vox_http.mli) hides `Internal`, `Reverse` and `Driver`; `http_private_rejected.ml` checks that boundary.

notes.title: The reachable-state invariant
notes.to: && (if observed state.core then core_wire state.core === prefix
notes.text: `reachable state prefix` says the budget accounts for exactly `prefix`, the accumulated lines and headers are valid, and, while no error has occurred, `core_wire` of the state is the consumed prefix itself. `feed_reachable` preserves it, and `reachable_completion` turns it into `well_formed request && serialize request === prefix` for a completed state.

notes.title: Chunking invariance in the model
notes.text: Feeding `left @ right` equals feeding `left` and then the leftover followed by `right`, proved by induction on `left` for every state, including terminal and budget-exhausted ones. The public `chunking_invariance` transfers this to driver states through `feed_machine` and `machine_injective`.

notes.title: Completeness: serialized requests parse back
notes.text: For a `well_formed` request, `serializer_core_roundtrip` shows the unbudgeted `drain` reaches `Complete request` on `serialize request`; `feed_matches_drain` shows the budgeted `feed` agrees because the request fits the budget; `chunking_invariance` and terminal preservation then add an arbitrary suffix, which is returned unconsumed.

notes.title: Soundness for arbitrary input
notes.text: From `initial ()` and any input, the reached state is `reachable` for the consumed prefix, so a completed request is `well_formed`, its serialization is exactly the consumed bytes, and it followed by the returned rest is the input. No assumption about where the input came from is involved.

notes.title: Driver: the executable machine
notes.text: `push` mirrors `Model.step` with accumulators consed at the head and `Reverse.rev` applied once when a line or body completes; `consume` mirrors `Model.feed`. The public `feed` runs `consume`, so this is the parser's running code.

notes.title: Simulation of the model by the driver
notes.text: For every driver state and input, `model` of the state `consume` reaches equals the state `Model.feed` reaches from `model s`, and the leftover inputs are equal; the per-byte step is `step_simulation`. This lemma connects every model theorem to the code that runs.

notes.title: The public feed
notes.text: `run` executes `Driver.consume` and returns its state and untouched suffix. The erased simulation proof establishes the single public contract: these observations equal the result of `Model.feed`.

what.short: Reader's guide to the RSA demo: domain and public claims, the review order, the trust statement, and an outline of the proof across the four implementation files.
long: Documentation for [RSA](demo:rsa). It states the public guarantees of `modexp` and `roundtrip_correct`, lists the review surface in order (`stdlib/bigint.mli`, `vox_rsa_spec.ml`, `vox_rsa_spec.mli`, `vox_rsa.mli`, itself), and outlines the proof: exponent and remainder laws in `vox_rsa_arithmetic.ml`, extended Euclid and CRT uniqueness in `vox_rsa_number_theory.ml`, Fermat's little theorem in `vox_rsa_fermat.ml`, and the round trip and CRT decryption in `vox_rsa.ml`.

It states that the demo assumes no arithmetic facts and adds no trusted RSA primitives, which holds at HEAD: the five RSA source files contain no `external`, no `assume_` and no statement without proof. It also records that the tests omit `-principal` because of a `Bigint` access-mode coercion in the ghost proof.

what.short: The RSA definitions: power by repeated multiplication, primality by trial division, Euclid's gcd, lcm, lambda p q = lcm (p - 1) (q - 1), and valid_key.
long: Defines `power`, `no_divisors`, `prime`, `gcd`, `lcm`, `lambda` and `valid_key` over `Bigint.t`, each as a `let[@def]` so the checker generates its defining equation; the recursive ones carry a `[@@decreases ...]` measure. The conventions matter when reading the claims: `power a e` is 1 for `e <= 0`, `gcd` returns 0 for a negative argument, `lcm` returns 0 for a nonpositive one, and `Bigint`'s `mod` is Euclidean.

These are the definitions every public claim of [RSA](demo:rsa) is stated in; clients see them as `Vox_rsa.Spec`. The file is verified (totality and termination are checked) and is independent of RSA: `prime` is trial division, with no reference to Fermat or to the proofs.

notes.title: Primality and the key condition
notes.text: `prime p` holds when `p > 1` and no integer in [2, p - 1] divides it. `valid_key p q e d` is exactly the premise of the round-trip theorem: two distinct primes, positive exponents, and `e * d - 1` divisible by `lambda p q`.

what.short: The RSA definitions as checked equations: power_def, no_divisors_def, prime_def, gcd_def, lcm_def, lambda_def and valid_key_def.
long: Declares each definition of [vox_rsa_spec.ml](src:verification/library/vox_rsa_spec.ml) as a total function together with a lemma stating its defining equation; the compiler checks the implementation against it, so the equations are verified. It exports no proof machinery.

It is part of the review surface of [RSA](demo:rsa): `vox_rsa.mli` aliases it as `Spec`, and clients call the `_def` lemmas to unfold `prime` or `valid_key` when proving preconditions, as `rsa_public_client.ml` does.

what.short: Repeated-squaring modexp over Bigint with its exact refinement, and the exponent and remainder laws the rest of the RSA proof uses.
long: `modexp` is the executable function behind `Vox_rsa.modexp`, `encrypt` and `decrypt`: it recurses on `e / 2`, squares, and multiplies by `a mod n` when `e` is odd, with `[@@decreases exponent]`. Its result is refined to `0 <= r < n && r = power a e mod n`. The ghost lemmas are `power_add`, `power_multiply`, `reduce_power`, `reduce_product`, `reduce_left`, `remainder_unique`, `divides_sum`, `divides_transitive`, `multiply_congruent`, `multiply_four` and `equal_remainders`.

Part of [RSA](demo:rsa); verified, with no externals or assumptions. The module has no interface, so all its lemmas are visible to the other RSA modules; `vox_rsa.mli` exports only `modexp` and its aliases. The catalogue notes that `reduce_power` exceeds the slow-refinement warning threshold on x86-64.

notes.title: remainder_unique
notes.text: Any decomposition `a = n * q + r` with `0 <= r < n` determines `a mod n = r`. The proof splits on how `q` compares with `a / n`. Almost every modular fact in the RSA proof is reduced to this lemma by supplying the right quotient explicitly, which keeps the nonlinear arithmetic within the solver's reach.

notes.title: Repeated squaring and its invariant
notes.text: With `k = e / 2`, the recursive call gives `half = power a k mod n`; `power_add` and `reduce_product` give `square = power a (2k) mod n`, and in the odd case `power_def` and `reduce_product` give `power a e mod n`. The asserted units `(() : {u : unit | ...})` state these intermediate facts, and all proof calls are in `ghost_`.

what.short: Extended Euclid with Bézout coefficients, and from it prime cancellation, the lcm properties and uniqueness in the Chinese remainder theorem.
long: `extended_gcd` returns a ghost record `bezout = {g; x; y}` with `g = gcd a b = a * x + b * y` and `g` dividing both inputs. `no_divisors_at` and `prime_divisors` turn trial-division primality into the fact that a prime's only positive divisors are 1 and itself; `prime_coprime` gives a Bézout identity `1 = a * x + p * y`; `prime_cancel` is Euclid's lemma (for `a >= 0` with `a mod p <> 0`, if `p` divides `a * b` it divides `b`). `lcm_properties` proves `lcm` is a positive common multiple dividing every common multiple, and `crt_unique` proves that two values in [0, p * q) with the same residues modulo distinct primes are equal.

Part of [RSA](demo:rsa); all functions are `@ ghost` lemmas, verified, with no externals or assumptions. `prime_cancel` suppresses the slow-refinement warning; its comment records about 15.6 million solver resource units.

notes.title: Extended Euclid
notes.text: Recursion follows `Spec.gcd` exactly, so `gcd_def` connects the two, and the coefficients are updated as `(y, x - (a / b) * y)`. The result is a ghost value: the record is erased together with the call.

notes.title: Euclid's lemma
notes.to: divides_sum p (a * b) p r.x (r.y * b);
notes.text: From `1 = a * x + p * y`, `b = (a * b) * x + p * (y * b)`, and `divides_sum` shows `p` divides it. This is the most expensive goal in the demo, hence the suppressed `slow-refinement` warning.

notes.title: CRT uniqueness
notes.text: If `a` and `b` agree modulo `p` and modulo `q`, then `q` divides `a - b`, and `prime_cancel` shows `p` divides `(a - b) / q`, so `p * q` divides `a - b`; both lying in [0, p * q) forces `a = b`. `rsa_power` and `decrypt_crt_correct` in `vox_rsa.ml` rely on it.

what.short: Fermat's little theorem for every prime, proved by showing that multiplication by a unit permutes the nonzero residues, then extended to exponents 1 + k(p - 1).
long: Defines ghost list functions `count`, `product`, `remove`, `interval` and `multiples`, and proves `product_extensional` (two lists in which every value occurs equally often have equal products). `multiples_count` and `multiples_permute` show that `a * 1, ..., a * (p - 1)` modulo `p` is a permutation of `1, ..., p - 1` when `a` has an inverse; `multiples_product` relates its product to `power a (p - 1)` times `(p - 1)!`; `interval_product_nonzero` shows `(p - 1)!` is not divisible by `p`. `fermat_little` cancels it to get `power a (p - 1) mod p = 1`, `fermat` gives `power a p mod p = a mod p` for every integer `a`, and `fermat_period` gives `power a (1 + k * (p - 1)) mod p = a mod p` for `k >= 0`.

Part of [RSA](demo:rsa), where `fermat_period` is applied at each prime in the round-trip proof and `fermat_little` justifies the inverse used by `decrypt_crt`. All lemmas are `@ ghost`, verified, with no externals or assumptions.

notes.title: Equal counts give equal products
notes.text: The hypothesis is a total proof function `equal_counts` giving `count x xs = count x ys` for every `x`. The induction removes the head of `xs` from `ys` and builds a new such function, `same`, for the tails. This replaces a permutation argument with counting.

notes.title: Fermat's little theorem
notes.text: For `a >= 0` not divisible by prime `p`: the Bézout coefficient from `prime_coprime` is an inverse, so the multiples of `a` permute the nonzero residues, hence `power a (p - 1) * f` and `f` agree modulo `p` for `f = (p - 1)!`, and `prime_cancel` removes `f`.

notes.title: The periodic form used by RSA
notes.text: Induction on `k` using `fermat` (valid for every integer, including multiples of `p`) and `period_step`. This is the fact applied at `p` and at `q` in `rsa_power`, which is why the round trip holds for messages divisible by either prime.

what.short: RSA on top of modexp: encrypt, decrypt, the round-trip theorem for distinct primes via Fermat and CRT, and CRT decryption with a proved recombination.
long: `encrypt` and `decrypt` are `modexp`. `rsa_power` proves `power m (e * d) mod (p * q) = m` under the key conditions: `lambda_lcm` shows `p - 1` and `q - 1` divide `e * d - 1`, `fermat_period` applies at each prime, and `reduce_divisor` with `crt_unique` combines the two congruences. `roundtrip_correct` adds `reduce_power` and `power_multiply` to reach the statement about `power (power m e mod (p * q)) d`, and `roundtrip` runs encryption then decryption and returns the plaintext refined equal to the message. `decrypt_crt` computes residues modulo `p` and `q` with `modexp`, computes the inverse of `p` modulo `q` as `modexp p (q - 2) q` (justified by `prime_inverse` and `computed_inverse_correct`), and recombines with `recombine`, proved by `recombine_correct` and `decrypt_crt_correct`.

This is the top of [RSA](demo:rsa); [vox_rsa.mli](src:verification/library/vox_rsa.mli) exports `modexp`, `encrypt`, `decrypt`, `roundtrip_correct`, `roundtrip` and `decrypt_crt`. It is verified and, together with the four other RSA modules, adds no assumptions: there is no `external`, no `assume_` and no statement without proof, so the demo trusts only the shared base, notably the built-in meaning of `Bigint`. The RSA modules are absent from `build.sh`; they are verified when the tests (`rsa.ml`, `rsa_rejected.ml`, `rsa_public_client.ml`) compile them from source.

notes.title: The core congruence
notes.to: crt_unique p q (a mod (p * q)) m)
notes.text: With `k = e * d - 1`, `k / (p - 1)` and `k / (q - 1)` are the periods passed to `fermat_period`, giving `m^(e*d)` congruent to `m` modulo each prime; `crt_unique` then identifies `m^(e*d) mod (p * q)` with `m`, which lies in [0, p * q).

notes.title: The round-trip theorem and its executable use
notes.text: `roundtrip_correct` is a ghost lemma stated for any integers under `valid_key` and `0 <= m < p * q`. `roundtrip` runs the real `encrypt` and `decrypt` and calls the lemma inside `ghost_`, so its result type `{r : t | r = message}` is proved about the values computed; no power is evaluated at run time for the proof.

notes.title: CRT decryption
notes.to: ghost_ (decrypt_crt_correct ciphertext d p q r);
notes.text: Uses the full exponent modulo each prime, without reducing it modulo `p - 1` and `q - 1`. The inverse of `p` modulo `q` comes from `modexp` with exponent `q - 2`, and `decrypt_crt_correct` proves the recombined value equals `power ciphertext d mod (p * q)` for every `d >= 0`.

what.short: Reader's guide to the Myers diff demo: how to run it, the two-interface review surface, the public guarantees, the algorithm and proof outline, and resource limits.
long: Documentation for [Myers diff](demo:myers-diff). It names `vox_diff_spec.mli` and `vox_diff.mli` as the complete review surface, explains the meaning of `Keep`, `Delete` and `Insert`, the 1,000,000-element limit and the tie policy, and outlines the private proof in [vox_diff.ml](src:verification/library/vox_diff.ml): the script lower bound, suffix cropping, frontier dominance, snake preserving remaining distance, and a ghost budget that decreases at each search step.

It also derives, informally, bounds on levels, snake calls and output length, and states that these are not a mechanized cost theorem, and it describes what the boundary, rejected and runtime tests check.

what.short: Implementation of the edit-script equations; minimum_cost is a fuel-bounded distance, and minimum_cost_equation proves the fuel-free recurrence the interface states.
long: Implements `source`, `target`, `cost`, `apply`, `invert`, `size` and `script_size` as `let[@def]` recursions, proves `apply_characterization` by induction, and defines `minimum_cost old fresh` as `distance` with fuel `size old + size fresh`. `minimum_cost_equation` proves that this satisfies the recurrence stated in [vox_diff_spec.mli](src:verification/library/vox_diff_spec.mli), which hides `distance` and the fuel.

Part of [Myers diff](demo:myers-diff); verified, with no externals or assumptions. The lemmas here are ordinary total functions that return `unit`, declared without `@ ghost`, so a caller that does not want them to run wraps the call in `ghost_`. `diff_rejected.ml` checks that clients cannot reach the private fuel.

notes.title: The distance with fuel
notes.text: Fuel makes the recursion decrease a single `Bigint` measure; a match costs two units and an edit one, so `size old + size fresh` suffices. The interface never mentions fuel: it states only the recurrence proved below.

notes.title: The recurrence, proved
notes.text: Unfolds `distance` once at full fuel and shows the recursive calls receive exactly the fuel `minimum_cost` would give the smaller inputs, so the fuel-free equation holds for all lists.

what.short: Edit scripts (Keep, Delete, Insert) and their meaning by equations: source, target, cost, apply, invert, size and the edit distance minimum_cost.
long: Declares the `operation` and `script` types and, for each function, a checked equation: `source_def`, `target_def`, `cost_def`, `invert_def`, `size_def`, `script_size_def`, `apply_characterization` (application succeeds exactly when the old list is the script's source, and yields its target) and `minimum_cost_equation` (the insertion/deletion distance by its recurrence, where a substitution costs two). Each equation recurses on shorter lists, so it determines its function.

First of the two files a reviewer reads for [Myers diff](demo:myers-diff); the claims in `vox_diff.mli` are stated only in these terms. The equations are verified against [vox_diff_spec.ml](src:verification/library/vox_diff_spec.ml).

notes.title: The edit distance
notes.to: then minimum_cost ats fresh else minimum_cost old bts))} @@ total
notes.text: Equal heads are kept at no cost; otherwise one plus the cheaper of deleting the old head or inserting the new one. This is the quantity `diff`'s result cost is proved equal to.

what.short: Myers' frontier search with erased proofs (snake, choose, advance, search, diff) and the lower bound that makes the computed script optimal against every script.
long: The private `Proof` and `M` modules hold the script reasoning: `restore_old`, `restore_new` and `reverse_into` for rebuilding a script from its reversed prefix, the `suffix` lemmas, `invert_correct`, `inverse_patch`, and in `M` the distance facts `neighbors`, `strip`, `crop`, `properties` and `lower_bound` (`minimum_cost (source s) (target s) <= cost s` for every script). A search `entry` is `{x; old_tail; new_tail; rev}`; the ghost predicate `valid old fresh k depth e` ties it to diagonal `k` and edit depth `depth`, and `dominance` shows that, on one diagonal, the entry further along the old input has no larger remaining distance. `Entry_proof`, `Choice_proof` and `Frontier_proof` collect the preservation lemmas.

The running code is `snake` (consume equal heads as `Keep`), `step_delete`, `step_insert`, `choose` (keep the candidate further along the old input, insertion on ties, then snake), `advance` (the next frontier, one slot wider), `finished` (find an entry with both tails empty and rebuild its script with `reverse_into`), `search` and `diff`. `search` terminates by `[@@decreases budget]` on a ghost budget that starts at `minimum_cost old fresh`; its invariant says some slot's remaining distance is within the budget, so it returns a script of cost at most `depth + budget`, and `lower_bound` in `diff` turns this into equality. `optimal_at` is `apply_characterization` plus `lower_bound`.

Verified, with no externals, no `assume_` and no statement without proof; [vox_diff.mli](src:verification/library/vox_diff.mli) hides every helper module. Part of [Myers diff](demo:myers-diff). The module is absent from `build.sh` and is verified when the tests compile it from source. That `diff` runs no proof code is checked by the Lambda audit in `diff_boundary.ml`; the tie rule is checked only by tests in `diff.ml`.

notes.title: The script lower bound
notes.to: | Insert b -> neighbors (source rest) (target rest) b b);
notes.text: Every script costs at least the distance between its source and target, by induction on the script: `Keep` uses the recurrence directly, and `neighbors` shows a one-element change moves the distance by at most one. This is the whole optimality argument for `optimal_at`, independent of the search.

notes.title: The entry invariant
notes.text: An entry's reversed script `rev` rebuilds `old` and `fresh` from its tails, the tails are suffixes, `x` counts consumed old elements and stays within the 1,000,000 cap, the length difference fixes the diagonal `k`, and `rev` costs exactly `depth`. The predicate is ghost; the runtime entry holds only `x`, the tails and `rev`.

notes.title: snake
notes.text: Follows a diagonal while heads are equal, adding `Keep`. The termination measure `remaining` is a ghost argument equal to the old tail's size, so no counter runs. The result is `settled` and has the same remaining distance, by the `a = b` case of the recurrence.

notes.title: Choosing between deletion and insertion
notes.text: Of the two candidates for a slot, the one with larger `x` is kept and insertion wins ties; `Choice_proof.selected` uses `dominance` to show a candidate within budget survives. The choice is then snaked, so every frontier slot is settled.

notes.title: search and its ghost budget
notes.text: Invariant: the frontier at depth `depth` is valid, has `depth + 1` slots, and some slot's remaining distance is at most `budget`. If no slot is finished, `frontier_budget` shows `budget > 0`, and `advance` keeps the invariant with `budget - 1` at `depth + 1`. The returned script costs at most `depth + budget`, which is `minimum_cost old fresh` from the initial call.

notes.title: diff
notes.to: let result : (script, error) result = Error Input_too_large
notes.text: `bounded_length` checks both inputs against 1,000,000, stopping after at most 1,000,001 cells; the initial entry is snaked and `search` starts with the ghost budget `minimum_cost old fresh`. `M.lower_bound`, `apply_source` and `script_bounds` run in `ghost_` and give the exact cost, `apply old s === Some fresh`, and the length bound.

what.short: Merge-sort comparison budget and logarithmic-height laws, stated separately from their proofs.
what.long: The equations define `height`, `power` and `budget`; `height_bound` and `height_minimal` characterize the ceiling of the base-two logarithm for positive sizes. The implementation proves these laws and supplies the ghost `bounded_int` helper used when splitting credit tokens.

what.short: Private member/representative bindings used to connect the forest proof to the public class-list model.
long: The public definitions are in vox_partition_classes.ml. The private binding model supports pointwise compression and linking proofs; grouping converts it to classes while preserving all partition observations and transition relations.

what.short: Private proof that the path forest projects to the pure partition and that imperative updates implement its operations.
long: `project` maps each path to `(head, root)`. The observation lemmas preserve membership, representatives and size; `valid` proves a valid pure partition from a valid complete forest. `add_singleton` relates allocation to the pure singleton operation. `refresh` and `find` prove exact projection equality after compression. `join` relates linking to `redirect`, and `union` composes the two finds and link to prove `merge_classes`. `Vox_union_find_online` uses these lemmas to connect its private forest transitions to the public transition relations in [online union-find](demo:online-union-find).

what.short: Implements imperative union-find through a pure relational snapshot specification and a separate Cost interface.
long: model projects the owned forest to a pure snapshot. create establishes empty; make_set establishes added; find returns the representative and establishes same; union establishes joined. The implementation chooses representatives by rank, while the public relation allows any member of the merged class. Cost retains exact events, charged work and inverse-Ackermann fee bounds.

what.short: Public pure partition snapshots as lists of (representative, others), with distinct members and relational transitions.
Derived laws for the concrete class-list partition model, separate from its definitions.
Verified correspondence between class lists and member/representative bindings.
Private grouping of member/representative bindings into distinct classes, preserving observations and transitions.
Proof that binding transitions respect equality of partition observations.
Pure incremental HTTP semantics: forward-order state, exact byte transitions, budget exhaustion and the untouched input suffix.
long: Defines the semantic machine used by [vox_http.mli](src:verification/library/vox_http.mli). Line grammar and framing come from [vox_http_spec.ml](src:verification/library/vox_http_spec.ml). The executable parser uses reversed accumulators; its simulation proofs remain private in [vox_http.ml](src:verification/library/vox_http.ml).

notes.title: The forward model's byte transition
notes.text: `step` rejects values outside 0–255, enforces CRLF and calls `finish_line` at each line end. `advance` charges one budget unit per byte; `feed` stops at a terminal state or returns `Limit Message_bytes` without consuming another byte when the budget is spent. The public parser contract specifies exactly this transition and returned suffix.
